articles.title: David Tepper Believes Bryce Young Can Still Win 'Multiple' Super Bowls For Panthers
articles.summary: Panthers owner David Tepper remains confident in quarterback Bryce Young's potential to bring Super Bowl titles to Carolina.
articles.body: When Carolina Panthers owner David Tepper traded up to draft quarterback Bryce Young with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 draft, he proclaimed the Alabama product was the guy who could bring the franchise "multiple" Super Bowl titles. With the 25-year-old Young entering his fourth season, Tepper hasn't wavered from that belief. "I think he has a lot of talent, and with the right weapons and the right situation, yeah," Tepper said in a rare news conference with reporters on Wednesday. Young is 14-30 as the team's starting quarterback and the Panthers have yet to sign him to a long-term contract extension. Young is under contract through 2027 after the team picked up his fifth-year option. Tepper declined to say if the Panthers have offered Young a long-term deal — one that would reaffirm the organization's believe that he is worthy of being a franchise quarterback. But Tepper is pleased with the way Young progressed in his third season, leading the Panthers to the NFC South title and snapping a seven-year playoff drought before losing 34-31 to the Los Angeles Rams in the first round of the playoffs. Young threw for 264 yards and a touchdown and also ran for a score against the Rams, but Carolina fell on a late touchdown pass from league MVP Matthew Stafford. Young beat the Rams earlier last season, and finished with the best statistical numbers of his career surpassing 3,000 yards passing with 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. "He has performed at a high level against high-level competition," Tepper said. "It seems to bring the best out in him. Bryce is the type of guy who doesn't feel the pressure. You saw that against the Rams twice (last year). When you see that, you know it's there. Can he bring it every single game? I know it's there." Young Can Lead Rallies, But Looking For Faster Starts Young has displayed an ability to rally the Panthers. He has 12 game-winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime in the past three seasons. Tepper said that's great, but now he'd like to see Young — and the Panthers as a team — start games faster. Young has also had trouble starting the season fast. He is 0-3 in Week 1 games and the Panthers have been outscored 97-30 in those defeats entering Sunday's home opener against the Chicago Bears. Young has not thrown for more than 161 yards in any of those games and has six interceptions with only two touchdown passes. Young said that starting fast has been a point of emphasis for the Panthers. "We have talked a lot about that as a team, as a unit and as an organization," Young said. "That comes with work. It's about having the best week possible and going into the game, with as much communication as we can and just being on the same page." Tepper likes Offensive Players Panthers Have Added Tepper has referred to Young as a point guard who can distribute the ball, but added he could have used more playmakers to work with in past years. Tepper believes the Panthers now have those. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has a season of experience after winning AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and Jalen Coker is looking like a legitimate No. 2 receiver. The jury is still out on talented, but underachieving 2024 first-round draft pick Xavier Legette, but the Panthers added free agent veteran Darren Waller to give Young a pass-catching tight end. The Panthers have Chuba Hubbard in the backfield and are hoping Jonathon Brooks can overcome his knee injury and can give the team a big-play threat in the backfield. Tepper also thinks the team's overall depth has improved, pointing to the team's 3-1 record in the preseason. "We are more of a playoff team this year than we were last year," Tepper said. "I think the pieces are there and we have everything we need." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Inspiring story on fatherhood: How Tom Brady broke down in tears over fatherhood and what he did next changed everything
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, every major NFL passing record, and a career that most athletes can only dream of. But in a 2022 episode of ESPN.
articles.body: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, every major NFL passing record, and a career that most athletes can only dream of. But in a 2022 episode of ESPN's documentary series "Man in the Arena," none of that seemed to matter. Fighting back tears, Brady admitted something that no championship trophy could fix: "I know I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad's been to me." It was a rare, unscripted moment from a man famous for emotional control. And it turned out to be the beginning of something far more meaningful than a game plan.How did Tom Brady's own father shape his approach to fatherhood?The answer to that question starts decades before any Super Bowl. Tom Brady has spoken repeatedly about Tom Brady Sr., describing him as his "biggest supporter," "best friend," and "number one teacher." In 2017, a young fan asked Brady to name his hero at a Super Bowl interview. He paused, got visibly emotional, and said, "I think my dad is my hero because he's someone I look up to every day."That wasn't performance. Brady Sr. was at every game, every milestone. His presence was total. And that's precisely what made Brady feel inadequate when he looked at his own children. His career demanded relentless travel, film study, and physical preparation. The guilt was real.What Brady did with that guilt, though, is what separates the story from a familiar athlete sob story. He used it as a measuring stick. On Father's Day 2025, when that tearful 2022 clip resurfaced widely on social media, Brady reposted it and wrote, "Meant it then and mean it more than ever today." He followed it an hour later with a full tribute post to his father, crediting him with instilling "hard work, integrity, compassion and unconditional love" into the Brady family's foundation.How does Tom Brady balance being a good dad after his divorce from Gisele Bundchen?Brady and Gisele Bundchen finalized their divorce in October 2022. He shares son Jack, now 18, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan, and son Benjamin, 16, and daughter Vivian, 13, with Bundchen.On paper, co-parenting across two former relationships while managing a post-NFL media career sounds messy. In practice, Brady has made the kids his organizing principle. In January 2025, he posted a photo of all three together, writing, "I couldn't have imagined a better way to ring in the new year than with the loves of my life." Earlier this year, he flew Benjamin and Vivian to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics, posting that "relationships are built on shared experience" and joking he "won the gold medal for pizza" on the trip.He has also been openly self-critical in a way that feels genuine rather than calculated. At the 2024 Fortune Global Forum, Brady told a room full of executives that parenting is "probably the hardest job all of us have" and admitted he has "screwed up a lot." That candor carries weight precisely because it comes from someone who spent two decades obsessing over perfection.What does Tom Brady say makes a great father?This is where Brady's thinking gets interesting. In his July 2025 weekly newsletter, he made a distinction that few would expect from a seven-time champion: "Being a great football player didn't make me a great dad, but how I became a great player certainly had an impact."The work ethic, the accountability, the daily commitment to getting better. Those transferred. He wrote, "I think part of being a great father is being a great example of doing what it takes to take care of your family. I chose to do it by playing football."He's also honest about how long it took him to find his footing. In an appearance on "DeepCut with VicBlends," Brady said, "You get better as a parent, I think, because when you're a young parent, you don't really know what you're doing. You're winging it." He talked about constantly asking himself: "Am I listening or am I talking? Am I mentoring or am I disciplining? Am I holding them accountable or am I letting them get away with things?"These aren't the words of a man coasting on legacy. They're the words of someone still doing the work, just in a different arena.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What happened to Sam Darnold? Seahawks QB suffers injury scare after taking a sack in season opener against Patriots
articles.summary: NFL News: Seattle's Super Bowl banner had barely been unveiled at Lumen Field when the night took a sharp, uncomfortable turn. On the fifth play of the 2026 NFL.
articles.body: Seattle's Super Bowl banner had barely been unveiled at Lumen Field when the night took a sharp, uncomfortable turn. On the fifth play of the 2026 NFL season, quarterback Sam Darnold took a sack from former Seahawk Dre'Mont Jones on third-and-6 and came up visibly limping. He left the field without assistance but was soon inside the blue medical tent, and moments later was escorted to the locker room. The Seahawks listed him as questionable to return with a hip injury. Drew Lock took over. Just like that, the mood at Lumen Field changed entirely.How did Sam Darnold get injured in the Seahawks' Week 1 game?Seattle's opening drive had started with real promise. A 13-yard run from Jadarian Price, followed by a 13-yard completion to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, had the crowd buzzing. Then a George Holani run set up a second-and-one, before a penalty and an incompletion pushed it to third-and-6. That's when things unraveled.It was a coverage sack. Darnold pulled the ball down and tried to extend the play, but Dre'Mont Jones got to him and dropped him hard. Darnold came up limping. What made it sting even more was who delivered the hit. Jones had spent three seasons in Seattle before signing elsewhere and returned Wednesday night wearing Patriots colors.NBC sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung described exactly what she saw: "You could see Sam flanked there by the team's head trainer and their head orthopedic surgeon. When Sam first came off the field, he was waving the training staff off. You could see him digging his right hand into his right hip, trying to keep it loose. By the time the trainer talked him into going into the blue tent for evaluation, Sam started to limp. You could see him as he left the field. He's now in the X-ray room."Darnold completed one of his two passes for 13 yards before exiting the game. Hardly the start anyone in Seattle had in mind.What does Sam Darnold's injury mean for the Seahawks' championship defense?This is where the real concern sits. Darnold is not just a quarterback. He is the spine of everything Seattle built last season. He recorded 323 completions for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions during the 2025 regular season, and guided the Seahawks all the way to a Super Bowl title over these same Patriots. Losing him, even temporarily, reshuffles everything.Drew Lock, who takes over in his absence, appeared in five games for Seattle last year but barely contributed. His 2025 stat line reads: two completions from three attempts for 15 yards, and six rushing attempts for negative six yards. That is the man now running the offense for the defending champions.It is also worth noting that Seattle is trying to become just the tenth team in NFL history to win back-to-back Super Bowls. Only two teams this century have managed it: the 2003-04 Patriots and the 2022-23 Chiefs. Darnold's health is central to whether that conversation stays realistic.Last season, Darnold dealt with a left oblique issue in the lead-up to the NFC Divisional Round against the 49ers but was still healthy enough to play through it. This hip situation is different. X-rays were ordered. The locker room visit happened mid-game. There is no clear timeline yet.For now, Seattle is playing on and hoping for good news. The answers, though, will come later.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “A year ago from today, I thought about taking my own life” - How A.J. Brown turned small-town Mississippi roots into NFL dominance and mental health advocacy
articles.summary: NFL News: A.J. Brown has built an NFL career on strength, speed and the ability to make difficult catches look easy. But one of the most important parts of his .
articles.body: A.J. Brown has built an NFL career on strength, speed and the ability to make difficult catches look easy. But one of the most important parts of his story happened away from the field. During the 2020 season, when he was a rising star with the Tennessee Titans, Brown was dealing with depression and suicidal thoughts. In 2021, he first time publicly spoke about reaching that point and encouraged people to talk to someone when they are struggling. His journey from Starkville, Mississippi, to NFL stardom also includes family, fatherhood and a strong belief in helping others.What did A.J. Brown’s childhood in Starkville, Mississippi teach himLong before A.J. Brown became an NFL star, his life in Starkville, Mississippi, was shaped by his family and sports. Brown was born on June 30, 1997, and grew up playing both football and baseball. He attended Starkville High School, where he became one of the most highly regarded young athletes in the state.His father, Arthur Brown Sr., had a strong connection to baseball and helped create a baseball field for his children on the family’s large property. Brown’s mother is Josette Robertson. His parents placed importance on discipline and hard work while he was growing up.Brown also faced difficult moments during his teenage years. In a later conversation reported by ESPN, he spoke about his parents separating when he was around 11 or 12. He said he struggled with the change and acted out. He failed seventh grade and said he briefly became involved with the Gangster Disciples.Sports eventually became a major way for him to change direction. Brown played football, baseball and basketball, and his talent quickly made him stand out. At Ole Miss, he became one of the top wide receivers in college football before entering the NFL.The path was not as simple as a straight rise to fame. There were problems along the way, but Brown has also spoken about the people who helped him find a better direction.When did A.J. Brown reveal his struggle with depression and suicidal thoughtsBrown’s mental-health battle became public in November 2021, although he said the darkest period had come during the 2020 NFL season. At that time, he was playing for the Tennessee Titans and was already establishing himself as one of the league’s top young receivers.From the outside, his career appeared to be moving quickly in the right direction. Behind that success, however, Brown was struggling with depression and anxiety.In a video shared on social media, Brown spoke openly about how serious things had become.“A year ago from today, I thought about taking my own life. I had no more hope of better days, and everything was just going wrong for me. I didn’t think depression was real until it happened to me. But now I know it’s really real. I’m still here, I’m still going, I’m still smiling, and I’ve got a lot of things to be grateful for. Be there for someone because someone was there for me.”The message was important because Brown was not speaking as someone removed from the pressures of professional sport. He was a young NFL player in the middle of a successful season, yet he was privately dealing with thoughts that could have cost him his life.Brown also urged people to speak with someone instead of keeping their pain to themselves. The Tennessee Titans reported his message at the time and noted that he wanted others to take depression seriously.Reports also said fellow NFL player Elijah Moore checked on Brown during that period. Brown later described Moore as someone he considered like family.How did fatherhood change A.J. Brown’s view of lifeFamily became an important part of Brown’s life as his football career continued. His daughter Jersee was born in May 2020, around the same period as the mental-health struggles he later discussed publicly. Brown has previously spoken about how important his daughter was to him during that difficult period.Brown also has a son, Arthur Juan Brown Jr., who was born in September 2022. The children have remained a visible part of his life away from football.Brown’s family has changed further in recent years. He married Kelsey Riley in May 2026 after the couple became engaged in 2025. Riley is a former Texas Southern softball player, and the couple have two children together: Jersee and A.J. Jr.Fatherhood has also given Brown a reason to think beyond football. His career has included big contracts, major games and individual success, but his public comments about mental health show another side of his life. For him, being present for his children is part of what matters when the noise around his football career fades.Why does A.J. Brown’s mental-health message still matter todayBrown’s story stands out because his struggles happened while his NFL career was taking off. He was not someone who had disappeared from the public eye or stopped performing. He was an athlete many people saw as successful, yet he was dealing with serious emotional pain away from the field.That is the part of his story that continues to matter. His message was simple: talk to someone, listen to people around you and do not assume that depression is not real simply because someone looks successful.A.J. Brown has since continued to build his football career. He became a major part of the Eagles’ offense after his 2022 trade from Tennessee and helped Philadelphia win Super Bowl LIX in the 2024 season. In 2026, Philadelphia traded him to the New England Patriots.His football résumé is now filled with major achievements, but the most personal part of his story remains the decision to speak honestly about a period when he did not know how things would turn out.That openness is what gives his story meaning beyond football. Brown learned that being strong does not always mean handling everything alone. Sometimes, it means admitting that something is wrong and allowing another person to help.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How the Dianna Russini saga forced Mike Vrabel to publicly choose between his marriage and his media relationships
articles.summary: NFL News: Mike Vrabel walked into his first Patriots season carrying more than a new playbook. Photos of him with ESPN reporter Dianna Russini surfaced earlier .
articles.body: Mike Vrabel walked into his first Patriots season carrying more than a new playbook. Photos of him with ESPN reporter Dianna Russini surfaced earlier this year, setting off a chain of events that dragged his personal life into NFL headlines. Vrabel publicly declared his love for wife Jen, skipped part of the draft to attend counseling, and The Athletic launched a full standards review of Russini's coverage. Before a single regular-season snap, Vrabel was already managing a crisis that had nothing to do with football.Did Mike Vrabel and Jen Vrabel stay together after the Dianna Russini controversy?Yes. And Vrabel made sure people knew it.When reporters asked him about balancing family and coaching responsibilities back in May, he did not dodge the question or pivot to football talk. He answered directly. "Oh, really good. Again, I appreciate it. My family is great," Vrabel told reporters on May 27. "I love Jen. I love the boys. I love my personal friends. And then, this spring is focused on really the coaching staff. The players, more importantly than the coaching staff."That statement landed in a specific context. Page Six had already published photos of Vrabel and Russini together. Speculation was running hot. So when Vrabel said those words publicly, it was not a routine media availability answer. It was a deliberate message.What made it even more pointed was what happened around the same time. Vrabel told his staff he would miss Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft to focus on family counseling. For a first-year head coach with everything to prove in New England, voluntarily stepping away from the draft is not a casual decision. It signals where his priorities actually sat when things got uncomfortable.Then, in August, Vrabel and Jen were spotted together at the Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce wedding. That kind of public appearance, at that kind of high-profile event, after months of tabloid noise, said more than any statement could.What did The Athletic's investigation find about Dianna Russini's coverage of Mike Vrabel?The Athletic's internal standards review, published September 3, largely cleared Russini of producing biased reporting. But it did not let her off the hook entirely.The report found that Russini failed to disclose a clear conflict of interest to her editors. "As stated several times in this report, Russini did not disclose to her editors a clear conflict of interest," wrote The Athletic's Mike Semel. "The Athletic's standards on these issues are robust, but are subject to employee honor, candor and transparency."That distinction matters. There is a real difference between a reporter shading coverage to protect a source and a reporter simply not telling her bosses about a personal relationship. The investigation concluded it was the latter. But in the court of public perception, that nuance gets lost fast.What the ESPN report added was a detail about Vrabel himself. According to sources, he initially wanted to issue a stronger statement defending Russini's reporting ethics when the photos first came out. He ultimately pulled back, settling for a more measured response that downplayed the situation. Whether that restraint helped or hurt him remains an open question.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel laments Drake Maye's 3 interceptions in loss to Seahawks: 'We want to be aggressive, not reckless'
articles.summary: Mistakes — most notably three late interceptions thrown by Drake Maye — doomed the Patriots down the stretch and allowed the Seahawks to rally for a 13-10 wi...
articles.body:
For most of three quarters Wednesday night, the New England Patriots were in control of their Super Bowl rematch with the Seattle Seahawks .

But mistakes — most notably three late interceptions thrown by Drake Maye — doomed the Patriots down the stretch and allowed the Seahawks to rally for a 13-10 win .

After the game, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was blunt about how the game was lost.

"We want to be aggressive and just not reckless," Vrabel told reporters in his postgame news conference.

Vrabel went on to say that "it's never just about one guy." But he stated the obvious later when discussing how the Patriots lost the game despite a strong showing on defense.

"You can't throw three interceptions," Vrabel said. "Drake knows that."

New England 's defense was stifling for much of the game, forcing punts on each of Seattle's first five possessions that didn't include the end of the first half. The Seahawks finally got on the board with a field goal in the final four minutes of the third quarter.

Then Maye's mistakes set them up for victory.

With 14:27 remaining and New England holding a 10-3 lead, Maye took an unnecessary risk with a deep ball into double coverage on second-and-9 from midfield. Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett picked Maye off inside Seattle's 10-yard line.

The interception set Seattle up for its only touchdown of the game, a 45-yard catch-and-run from Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba that tied the game at 10-10.

On the next New England drive, Maye turned the ball over again. After Romeo Doubs dropped a sure first down on a Maye deep ball on second down, Maye again looked downfield on third-and-14. This time, Seahawks safety Julian Love came away with the interception that set Seattle up for a go-ahead field goal.

Then, on the last New England drive of the game, Maye made perhaps his worst mistake of the night.

With the Patriots in range of a game-tying field goal, Maye forced a pass into the end zone on third-and-5 targeting Mack Hollins . Instead, he found Seattle cornerback Josh Jobe , who intercepted the ball and got both feet down by the sideline for a game-sealing interception. Maye threw the ball under pressure off his back foot.

Had Maye thrown the ball away, Patriots kicker Andy Borregales would have had a look at a 34-yard field goal with a chance to send the game to overtime.

It added up to three interceptions by Maye on New England's final three drives that ultimately cost the Patriots the game. It was a tough look for Maye against a Seahawks defense that was the only unit to intercept Maye multiple times last season.

Maye will now have 11 days to sit on the mistakes before a chance for redemption in a Week 2 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 20.

articles.title: Patriots Super Bowl Champion Delivers Brutal 9-Word Verdict on Mike Vrabel And Co. as New England Gets Exposed in Week 1 vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Former New England Patriots cornerback Jason McCourty pulled no punches when outlining his thoughts on the Patriots’ 13-10 defeat to the defending champion S...
articles.body:
Former New England Patriots cornerback Jason McCourty pulled no punches when outlining his thoughts on the Patriots' 13-10 defeat to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks in the 2026 NFL season opener.

In truth, the game looked like anything but the compelling Super Bowl rematch that many expected, with both sides struggling to find rhythm. However, a combination of a steely, resolute defense and a clutch second half from backup quarterback Drew Lock in relief of injured Sam Darnold secured a huge win for Seattle .

Patriots' Sloppy Defeat To Seahawks Forces Jason McCourty To Offer Brutal Critique

McCourty aimed a subtle shot at the Patriots coaching staff, particularly head coach Mike Vrabel, for sitting his starters throughout the preseason.

The former corner, now an analyst, issued a 9-word tweet that read : "You can tell starters didn't play in preseason."

Vrabel, a source of major off-field controversy, sat his starters throughout the preseason, citing injury risk and concerns about roster depth, while New England gave players such as Drake Maye and A.J. Brown work in joint practices instead. McCourty argues that decision may have been a misjudgment.

In fairness, preseason's always a balancing act. Coaches have to weigh the benefits of extra reps in exhibition games against keeping key guys fresh and injury-free ahead of a grueling 17-game season, not including the playoffs; it can be a catch-22.

However, to McCourty's point, sloppy mental mistakes plagued them throughout as Maye threw three uncharacteristic interceptions in possibly the worst game of his star-studded young career.

It also didn't help that key offseason acquisition A.J Brown went down with an ankle injury. Suddenly, the Patriots looked bereft of playmakers to help Maye, with second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson also out injured.

It's fair to say they didn't look particularly ready to play this game, especially on offense.

Furthermore, the Patriots failed to generate much of anything on offense, converting a disappointing 5/16 on third downs. Rhamondre Stevenson only averaged 2.8 yards per carry for 51 rushing yards against the Seahawks' massive defensive line.

With Brown out of the game, Maye's receivers struggled to gain separation from a lockdown secondary, forcing Maye to scramble and force plays downfield to disastrous consequences.

Maye's worst mistake came with New England in field-goal range on third-and-5 from Seattle's 16-yard line with 26 seconds left and a chance to tie the game.

Instead, Maye threw toward the end zone under pressure, and Josh Jobe intercepted the pass to seal Seattle's win.

While that was some questionable decision-making, Jobe also deserves credit for his toe-tap interception, which secured the Seahawks' dramatic win.

However, that ugly loss will set up a week of introspection for Maye, Vrabel, and the Pats organization, raising questions about whether starters should have gotten at least some preseason reps.

articles.title: Drake Maye’s debut reinforces why Matthew Stafford won MVP
articles.summary: It would have only taken 1 vote for Matthew Stafford to lose MVP to Drake Maye
articles.body:
Drake Maye could have won last season's MVP trophy if he had received just one more first place vote, but the Patriots quarterback's poor play on Wednesday night against the Seahawks only reinforced why he was not in the same class as winner Matthew Stafford . Maye was at his absolute worst in the NFL's first game of 2026, throwing three fourth quarter interceptions, including the game-loser, as New England left the door open to blow a 10-point lead to Seattle and drop the game 13-10.

It would be one thing if this was just one bad start by a great quarterback — Stafford will have bad games too — but it's really more that Maye was left exposed again and hasn't really performed at a replacement level since last year's playoffs began. That's when the Patriots stopped facing the easiest schedule that any team had faced in over 20 years and had to start putting up points against team that have good defenses.

As of Wednesday's loss, the Patriots are 0-12 with Drake Maye in the regular season against teams that have a winning record.

Again, just a vote separated Maye and Stafford in the MVP race. A vote.

After completing over 72% of his passes in the regular season with a 113.5 passer rating, Maye faced four of the best defenses in the NFL in the playoffs: The Chargers, Texans , Broncos, and Seahawks.

He completed just 58.3% of his passes and had a passer rating of 82.2. Maye was sacked an NFL playoff record 21 times and threw four interceptions and fumbled seven times. In the Super Bowl, Maye threw for 295 yards, but much of that came in garbage time after Seattle had built a 29-0 lead. He threw two interceptions, lost a fumble, and was sacked six times.

Now compare that to Matthew Stafford in three games against the Seahawks last year:

Over 9.5 yards per attempt in his most recent two games

Facing the Seahawks on Wednesday, a defense that didn't have star nickel Nick Emmanwori or starting strong safety Ty Okada , Maye went 0-of-4 on passes over 20 yards with three interceptions, and 3/9 passing on throws over 10 yards:

He was a check down charlie and this all came after an entire offseason spent by New England of trying to build an offense around Maye that would finally click against better teams, not just the Jets and Dolphins. That included upgrading the offensive line with signings like Alijah Vera-Tucker, and bringing in new weapons like A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs .

And although Brown did leave the game in the second half with an ankle injury, Maye still wasn't playing that well before he got hurt. Basically A.J. Brown was the offense prior to his injury, not Drake Maye.

It is also true that Doubs dropped an easy pass that should have been a big gain for Maye. But when is Maye going to pick up the offense? He's supposed to be a dual threat quarterback and an accurate passer with a big arm, that's why the Patriots drafted him third overall in 2024. At times, he's even lived up to it. Or appeared to.

But at no point last season did it really feel like he belonged in the MVP conversation. Not against the easiest schedule in the NFL.

So it's fine to say that you like Drake Maye as an up and coming player (I do), or that the Patriots had lesser weapons and offensive support around the quarterback last season than the Rams (they did), but "MVP"?

Albert Breer voted for him . Gregg Rosenthal said Maye should be the MVP. Field Yates called Maye the MVP, as did most of ESPN. And almost 50% of the AP's panel of 50 writers who vote for MVP and other awards picked Maye.

It's hard to believe that almost happened and would have been the only reason Stafford didn't get his only MVP award so far. Because of Drake Maye and the easiest schedule in the NFL.

Wednesday just reinforced why the AP and the NFL got so lucky that it didn't.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 1 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: Like most fantasy football managers, you've probably tweaked your roster after drafts to find waiver-wire and free-agent gems.
articles.body:
Like most fantasy football managers, you've probably tweaked your roster after drafts to find waiver-wire and free-agent gems.

So, we're back with another year of the biggest weekly sleepers to target—players available in more than 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros .

The 2026 season is underway, with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers set to play Thursday night. Let's focus on Sunday's opening slate.

The list below includes two sleeper stacks and a veteran tight end who will be in a favorable matchup on his 34th birthday.

We'll highlight two players at each position and break down their matchups.

QB Tyler Shough at Detroit Lions (23 Percent Rostered)

Here's a reminder that Tyler Shough finished as QB9 or higher in fantasy scoring for three of the last five weeks of the 2025 season.

In one of those matchups, against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he didn't even throw a touchdown pass, but he ran for 55 yards and two scores. In the other two, the Saints signal-caller threw for 259-plus yards.

Add Shough now for the season. He should continue to improve as he gains experience in head coach Kellen Moore's offense.

In Week 1, the Saints will travel to face the Detroit Lions, who won't have All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph or Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch.

Even though Shough won't have explosive rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson, he can do enough damage to the Lions' undermanned secondary with Chris Olave, tight end Juwan Johnson and a sleeper wide receiver to be named below.

QB Malik Willis at Las Vegas Raiders (17 Percent Rostered)

In Malik Willis' only start last season, against the Baltimore Ravens, he threw for 288 yards, a touchdown and ran for 60 yards and two scores.

Although that's a small sample size, it's a glimpse at his upside.

After taking first-team reps as QB1 throughout the offseason, Willis could have a solid showing against a Las Vegas Raiders defense set to start rookie safety Treydan Stukes and second-year pro Darien Porter, who switched from wide receiver to cornerback at Iowa State two years ago.

Because of his rushing ability, Willis doesn't need to light up the Raiders defense for 300-plus yards to be a top-10 fantasy quarterback. He just needs about 200 yards and a splash of rushing production.

With five-time Pro Bowler Maxx Crosby coming off the edge, Miami Dolphins offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik will likely have a few designed quarterback runs in this weekend's game plan. Willis could rack up 300 yards passing and rushing combined, with a touchdown through the air and/or on the ground.

RB Keaton Mitchell vs. Arizona Cardinals (17 Percent Rostered)

Omarion Hampton is the Los Angeles Chargers' lead running back, but there's room for a flex-worthy pass-catcher out of the same backfield.

New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel values speed at the skill positions, so it's no surprise that the team signed Keaton Mitchell, who ran a 4.37 40-yard time coming out of East Carolina.

Mitchell tore his ACL at the end of his 2023 rookie campaign and didn't return to form until last season, when he played a backup role behind workhorse running back Derrick Henry.

Entering his second season, Hampton isn't nearly as established as Henry. Though he's slated to handle early-down carries, the 6'0", 220-pound tailback could cede touches to Mitchell on passing downs. If so, McDaniel can use the speedy running back for big gains in the short passing game.

With Mitchell returning to practice with limitations on Wednesday, make sure to monitor the Chargers' injury report to ensure he's ready to go for Sunday's favorable matchup.

Tracking NFL's Biggest Week 1 Injuries 🏥

RB Kaleb Johnson at Minnesota Vikings (5 Percent Rostered)

With Josh Jacobs out indefinitely on the commissioner's exempt list, the Green Bay Packers have listed MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks as their top two running backs, but the role projection matters more than the pecking order on the depth chart.

Lloyd will likely handle the majority of touches, but that's not a guarantee because of his injury history. He's appeared in just one game, logging six carries for 15 yards since the Packers selected him in the third round of the 2024 draft.

According to The Athletic's Matt Schneidman , Brooks is a pass-blocking running back with reliable hands.

"We pretty much know what Brooks is at this point: a great pass protector who's efficient with the ball in his hands in small doses," Schneidman wrote in a recent mailbag response.

If the Packers choose to be cautious with Lloyd's workload, Kaleb Johnson could take on a complementary early-down role. He's a 6'1", 224-pound downhill ball-carrier who accumulated 1,537 rushing yards and 21 touchdowns, earning All-American honors in his final collegiate season at Iowa.

Remember, the Packers traded a sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Johnson before the NFL announced it placed Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list. Green Bay may have a plan for Lloyd and Johnson to split carries. Even if Johnson doesn't see much playing time right away, he could plunge into the end zone on short-yardage opportunities.

WR Tre Tucker vs. Miami Dolphins (15 Percent Rostered)

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers will miss "a game or two" after undergoing a meniscus trim.

Without Bowers, one of the Raiders' receivers can emerge as the lead pass-catcher in first-year head coach Klint Kubiak's offense. Based on what transpired over the summer, Tre Tucker is the team's No. 1 wideout.

During organized team activities (OTAs) in June, Kubiak told reporters Tucker had taken on a leadership role in a young receiver room. Jalen Nailor is 27, but it's his first year in Las Vegas.

Tucker didn't see much action in the preseason, which is an indicator that he holds a secure spot atop the depth chart. In limited exhibition action, the fourth-year pro hauled in all five of his targets for 46 yards.

Going up against the Miami Dolphins' young, inexperienced secondary, Tucker should have a strong start to his 2026 campaign. He's seen a steady increase in catches and receiving yards every year in the league.

WR Devaughn Vele at Detroit Lions (4 Percent Rostered)

Devaughn Vele completes the New Orleans Saints sleeper stack. Quarterback Tyler Shough built a strong rapport with him at the end of last season, and they could pick up where they left off.

Between Weeks 13 and 15 of the 2025 campaign, Vele hauled in 16 of his 19 targets for 202 yards and a touchdown. The Saints placed the wideout on injured reserve with a shoulder injury, which sidelined him for the final three games of the season.

With rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, Vele should be the No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave in the Saints' passing game. Keep in mind that New Orleans traded a 2026 fourth-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Denver Broncos for him in head coach Kellen Moore's first year with the team.

As the Saints' offensive play-caller, Moore may try to get some return on the team's investment in Vele while Tyson recovers from injury.

TE Chig Okonkwo at Philadelphia Eagles (11 Percent Rostered)

Even though the Washington Commanders signed wideout Stefon Diggs, who will command a fair number of targets as the No. 2 receiver, the team inked Chig Okonkwo to a sizeable three-year, $40 million deal early in free agency.

As the immediate replacement for Zach Ertz, who was second on the team in targets for back-to-back years with Jayden Daniels under center, Okonkwo could be picking up a big role despite Diggs' late offseason arrival in Washington.

In a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Commanders could attack the middle of the field rather than target All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and free-agent acquisition Riq Woolen on the boundaries.

Washington could favor a one-on-one matchup featuring Okonkwo, an athletic pass-catching tight end, against second-year linebacker Jihaad Campbell, who was a part-time starter last season.

TE Darren Waller vs. Chicago Bears (2 Percent Rostered)

For those of you who remember the tail end of tight end Jimmy Graham's career, Darren Waller is at that stage—a top-tier, touchdown-dependent fantasy option.

For context, Graham scored 15 touchdowns over his last three seasons in the NFL and didn't reach 500 receiving yards in any of those campaigns.

Last year, Waller came out of retirement, and the New York Giants traded him to the Miami Dolphins. He caught 24 passes for 283 yards and six touchdowns, scoring four times in his first three games back on the field.

Waller turns 34 on the first Sunday of the NFL season. While age is a consideration, he enters Week 1 as the Carolina Panthers' lead tight end in an offense that needs a consistent playmaker at the position.

Waller's return bumped Tommy Tremble and Ja'Tavion Sanders down on the depth chart. Quarterback Bryce Young could find success targeting Waller, as he has developed a rapport with big-bodied wideout Tetairoa McMillan, who is listed at 6'4", 220 pounds on the team's official website .

Fantasy managers in need of an early-season starter at tight end should consider Waller for the first few weeks before age and workload become concerns. He's capable of scoring twice against the Bears, who are without starting safety Coby Bryant and slot cornerback Kyler Gordon.

NFL preseason statistics are provided by CBS Sports .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Tracking NFL's Biggest Week 1 Injuries After Brock Bowers' Surgery, Cowboys' Tyler Smith Lands on IR
articles.summary: The NFL regular season is an endurance race often decided by attrition. By the end of it, the healthiest teams often have the best chance of going on a deep playoff run.
articles.body:
The NFL regular season is an endurance race often decided by attrition. By the end of it, the healthiest teams often have the best chance of going on a deep playoff run.

The 2026 regular season got underway on Wednesday night. While injuries are usually more of a factor later in the year, we've already seen some significant ones that could impact early campaigns.

New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson missed the opener with an ankle injury. The Dallas Cowboys recently placed starting guard Tyler Smith on injured reserve (with a designation to return) following thumb surgery.

On Wednesday, we learned that the Las Vegas Raiders will be without star tight end Brock Bowers. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the talented pass-catcher underwent a meniscus trim on Tuesday and will miss "a game or two" while he recovers.

Here, we'll dive into some of the most notable injuries and injury recoveries worth tracking ahead of the remaining Week 1 slate. We'll examine the specifics of each situation, how Week 1 matchups could be impacted, and the latest buzz from around the league.

TE George Kittle and Edge Nick Bosa, San Francisco 49ers

The San Francisco 49ers will open their 2026 season on Thursday night with a brutal test. Not only will they have to battle a loaded Los Angeles Rams team, but they will also have to do so across the world in Melbourne, Australia.

The good news for the 49ers is that they may have two of their key playmakers back against the rival Rams. Pass-rusher Nick Bosa (torn ACL) and tight end George Kittle (torn Achilles) both suffered significant injuries last season that threatened to linger into 2026. However, both are trending toward availability.

On Tuesday, 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris told reporters that Bosa will be in the lineup, while offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said that Kittle's return is a distinct possibility.

"We have got to see how he gets through the rest of the week, we've got two more practices, but Kittle looks good," Kubiak said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner .

Fantasy managers will want to monitor Kittle up until the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, but Bosa should be a go. Having both would be a big boon to San Francisco's chances of outlasting the early Super Bowl favorites.

Fans won't get to see star Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald against the 49ers on Thursday night. While the three-time Defensive Player of the Year did end his retirement to return to L.A. this season, he isn't ready to take the field just yet.

Donald did not travel with the Rams to Melbourne.

Fans should, however, get a few glimpses of prized trade acquisition Myles Garrett. While the reigning Defensive Player of the Year has spent much of the summer managing swelling in his knee, he's set to make his debut for L.A. against the rival 49ers.

"He's looked great," Rams coach Sean McVay said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . "We've been smart with Myles, like I've kind of told you guys, but his impact has been tremendous."

The Rams may look to utilize Garrett on a limited snap count, but he should still have a big impact on their pass rush. Expect him to command regular double teams, which should open up playmaking opportunities for Byron Young, Kobie Turner, and Braden Fiske.

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took the league by storm as a rookie in 2024. However, he suffered a torn ACL last season that ended his campaign after only four games.

The Giants are banking on a return to form by Nabers as they look to compete under new head coach John Harbaugh and with second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart. While the LSU product may not be in full pre-injury form to face the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, he appears set to suit up.

"I think he's ready to go," Harbaugh said, per The Athletic's Charlotte Carroll . "...If he's ready to go, and he feels like he's ready to go, then he'll play."

If Nabers is back and close to 100 percent, it will allow New York to test Dallas' new-look defense early and often. If he isn't, the Giants will have to rely on a shallow receiver room. Odell Beckham Jr., Darnell Mooney, and Malachi Fields are the only other receivers on their active roster.

Arizona Cardinals fans have been eager to see the debut of rookie running back and third overall pick Jeremiyah Love .

The Notre Dame product looked impressive during his preseason debut on August 13, but he's been dealing with an ankle injury ever since.

The good news is that Love was back at practice this week, and head coach Matt LaFLeur said the rookie has had "no limit," according to NBC Sports' Kyle Dvorchak .

Having Love available will give Arizona a potent dual-threat option as it looks to upset the Los Angeles Chargers on the road. However, this doesn't mean the rookie is ready to be the focal point of the offense.

Love was listed as the No. 2 running back behind Tyler Allgeier on the Cardinals' Week 1 depth chart .

Realistically, fans can probably expect to see a good bit of both backs as Arizona opens the season with a committee approach.

Fans can add Bowers to the list of standouts they won't see in Week 1. While missing him will be big, it looks like Las Vegas should have standout running back Ashton Jeanty available when it hosts the Miami Dolphins on Sunday.

Jeanty had been out of practice with a low ankle sprain since suffering the injury on August 23. However, he returned to practice on Wednesday, and head coach Klint Kubiak has expressed optimism about his Week 1 availability, according to ESPN's Ryan McFadden .

Bowers' absence will likely mean an uptick in targets for backup tight end Michael Mayer against Miami. Whether Jeanty gets the start or not, fans should expect to see a good amount of rookie running back Mike Washington Jr .

Washington has the sort of breakaway speed that will complement Jeanty's physical playing style. Kubiak regularly rotated running backs Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet as the Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator.

WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Cincinnati Bengals

The Cincinnati Bengals are set to debut a new-look defense—one now headlined by defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence—on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

If Cincinnati cannot slow Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers, it may have to win a high-scoring game. That would be an incredibly daunting challenge if either Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins were to miss the game—and both have been dealing with injuries.

Chase has been dealing with a knee injury while Higgins has been battling a heel ailment. Neither is guaranteed to play or be at 100 percent on Sunday, but the dynamic duo is trending in the right direction.

"They continue to do more and more every day, but I like the pace they're on," head coach Zac Taylor said, per Geoff Hobson of the team's official website.

If Chase and/or Higgins is limited against Tampa, Cincinnati will likely look to lean on Chase Brown and its ground game while hoping that its rebuilt defense is as advertised.

WR Rome Odunze and RB D'Andre Swift, Chicago Bears

The Chicago Bears will open their season on Sunday against the defending NFC South champion Carolina Panthers. The Bears are looking to defend their own division title while making a deeper push into the postseason.

Unfortunately, two of Chicago's key offensive players are banged up heading into Week 1. Wideout Rome Odunze is dealing with a foot injury, while running back D'Andre Swift exited practice last week with cramps.

Running back Kyle Monangai has also been out of practice since mid-August with a knee injury.

However, Swift and Monangai both returned to practice on Tuesday, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. Both should be on hand to test Carolina's run defense on Sunday. The outlook is far less certain for Odunze:

If Odunze can't go, fans should expect to see a lot of Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, and Kalif Raymond in the passing game.

DT Nnamdi Madubuike and WR Zay Flowers, Baltimore Ravens

The Baltimore Ravens will open their season against the Indianapolis Colts in what will be the debut of new head coach Jesse Minter.

The availability of two notable players could shape whether Minter begins his Baltimore tenure with a win.

Standout receiver Zay Flowers has been dealing with a hamstring and was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice. Also limited was defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, who missed all but two games in 2025 with a neck injury.

It's been a long road back for Madubuike, who hasn't played in nearly a full calendar year. He may not be quite ready to return to live action against the Colts, though Minter won't rule out a Week 1 debut.

If Madubuike does return, even on a limited basis, it should help Baltimore's defense slow Daniel Jones, Jonathan Taylor, and the rest of Indy's offense. He was one of the league's most disruptive interior defenders before the injury.

If Flowers is limited, Ravens rookie third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane could take on a larger role in his NFL debut.

Week 1 will end with a Monday Night Football thriller between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs. Not only will the matchup provide a drama-drenched AFC West showdown, but it should also mark the return of Patrick Mahomes.

The Chiefs quarterback suffered a torn ACL roughly nine months ago. While he was cleared in time to participate in training camp, that never guaranteed that he'd be ready for regular-season action by Week 1.

Mahomes' return still isn't guaranteed, but it's looking incredibly likely.

"There's a pretty good chance Patrick will go ahead and start, unless something were to come up here in the next couple days," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said on Tuesday, per ESPN's Nate Taylor .

Justin Fields would serve as Kansas City's backup, but Patrick Mahomes appears set to start. Mahomes is returning from a significant knee injury, however, and Kansas City will face a difficult Denver defense in Week 1.

articles.title: Examining Fantasy Football Week 1 Trade Market for Top 50 Flex NFL Players
articles.summary: We are so back.
articles.body:
The NFL returns this week, and that means fantasy football returns as well. That also means it's time to start maniacally obsessing over your roster, trying to find every little advantage possible.

And thus returns the trade value chart. This early in the season, trade values are going to be determined solely on preseason ranks, and you may be hesitant to pull the trigger on any deals. Understandable. But if you had a wonky draft or just can't help but be transaction happy, we are here to assist.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

Gibbs and Robinson are essentially untouchable. Elite running backs are hard to come by, and this pair are firmly in their primes and could each be league-winners. If you lucked out and got either, trading them would be folly.

Chase, Nacua and Smith-Njigba are close behind in that regard, set to gobble up targets and post huge numbers yet again in exciting offenses. It was a very good year to have a top-five pick.

As for a player who perhaps was a bit undervalued this draft season and could be worth considering as an early-campaign trade target, don't sleep on Barkley. Sean Mannion's offensive scheme will prioritize more under-center formations, which should help Philly's run game, and the Eagles' offensive line appears to be healthy and ready to return to elite status in 2026.

Barkley had a down year by his own lofty standards in 2025, and at 29 concerns about a gradual decline in his ability are understandable. But last season's stale scheme and the injuries up front absolutely played a part in his regression too. Don't expect 2,000 rushing yards, but don't be surprised if he's a fantasy stud either.

On the other end of the spectrum, Mike McDaniel has continued to suggest that he'll use all three of his running backs in Los Angeles and may ride the " hot hand " throughout the season, a concern for second-year man Hampton.

If you believe Hampton's talent will lead him to being the hot hand more often than not, then hold on tight and reject any trade overtures. It remains the most likely outcome. But if he's firmly stuck in a three-way timeshare after a few weeks this season, his trade value is going to evaporate quickly.

articles.title: 49ers vs. Rams Updated Odds, Money Line, Spread, Props to Watch for TNF
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams do battle on Thursday night in the most unique season opener either franchise has ever experienced.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams do battle on Thursday night in the most unique season opener either franchise has ever experienced.

The NFC West rivals face off in Melbourne, Australia. The game will be played on Friday morning in Australia.

Much has been made about the strategies of each team in terms of getting to Australia. San Francisco made the trip last week, while Los Angeles traveled 48 hours before kickoff.

No one is sure if the travel difference will make much of a difference, but one thing is for sure, this should be a tight battle in which both teams need to start their seasons right.

The Rams are easier to forecast from a betting perspective because of their known quantities on offense.

The 49ers have a little bit of unknown to parts of their offense, which might be where bettors take advantage of some player prop bets.

Money Line: San Francisco (+176; bet $100 to win $176); Los Angeles (-210; bet $210 to win $100)

Both teams were strong against the spread in 2025. The Rams were 14-6 ATS, while the 49ers were 13-6.

The NFC West sides split their regular-season series last year. The 49ers won outright as an underdog in their win, while the Rams covered as a six-point favorite in their victory.

Both meetings last season went over. The first game had a total of 43.5, while the second game had an Over/Under of 49.5.

Kyren Williams was consistent in both of his meetings with the 49ers in 2025.

The Rams running back recorded 65 and 73 in the pair of divisional clashes. Both of those totals were recorded on 14 carries.

Williams is once again expected to receive a good amount of carries inside the Rams offense, which is why his Week 1 rushing-yard prop looks enticing.

Williams recorded at least 50 rushing yards in all but one game last season. He failed to make it over 55 rushing yards on just three occasions.

The 49ers defense is formidable, but Williams proved last season he can chip away at that unit.

Matthew Stafford went 24-for-36 and 30-for-47 against San Francisco a year ago.

He averaged 22.8 completions per game in the regular season. The importance on his accuracy is heightened in a divisional contest, so you'd think he gets over his projected mark on completions.

Stafford has the two best receivers in the contest in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. He also has a versatile tight end room to work with, led by Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee.

Stafford has had no problem spreading the ball around inside the Rams offense, and he'll have the chance to do that to kick off the season in Melbourne.

Christian McCaffrey Over 107.5 Rushing & Receiving Yards

The 49ers offense carries more unknowns than the Rams' unit.

Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and George Kittle are not officially on the injury report, but there are questions about their usage and health in Week 1.

Christian McCaffrey is the constant in the 49ers offense. It's easy just to take his props instead of risking it with the passing attack.

McCaffrey had 66 and 82 receiving yards in the two meetings with the Rams last season. He also ran for 87 yards in the two games.

A high usage rate is expected out of the 49ers' star running back, and with questions elsewhere, it's easy to go after his combined yards prop.

De'Zhaun Stribling Over 2.5 Receptions & Over 34.5 Receiving Yards

Rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling has the potential to be the breakout star in Thursday's game.

The rookie out of Ole Miss had a strong preseason. That could carry over into Week 1.

He may not lead the 49ers in any receiving category, but he can be a useful depth piece for Brock Purdy to look to.

The Rams will put more time into covering Evans, Samuel, Kittle and McCaffrey, so there should be some open spaces for the rookie to work in.

A three-catch, 35-yard game might not pop in the box score, but it would cash both of his receiving props.

He's the only offensive player on either side who you can justify taking a risk on with so many well-known players across the offensive skill positions.

articles.title: Oddsmakers react to the differing travel strategies for NFL game in Australia: 'My first thought is the Rams are nuts'
articles.summary: Is the Rams or 49ers' travel strategy better for a game in Australia? We asked handicappers and oddsmakers.
articles.body:
The NFL will play its first-ever regular-season game in Australia later this week when the Los Angeles Rams "host" the San Francisco 49ers as 3.5-point favorites. The game will kick off at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday night here in the United States, but will be played at 10:35 a.m. local time on Friday morning in Melbourne. Both teams will take at least a 16-hour flight to get there — although Aaron Donald won't have to make the trip , as he was ruled out for the game on Tuesday.

To further add intrigue to the game, the teams consulted with their staffers and arrived at diametrically opposed travel strategies. The 49ers flew out on Sept. 2, and will be in Australia for about a week prior to the game, while the Rams plan to fly into Melbourne the day before the game and fly out immediately afterwards.

While the Rams are the clear Super Bowl favorite , no preseason favorite with +500 or better odds has ever won the Super Bowl over the past 30 seasons (0-for-20). And no preseason Super Bowl favorite has ever had to start its season this many time zones away on another continent — against a division opponent that could have an impact on the NFC West and No. 1 seed.

Variance provides opportunity in sports betting, and it would stand to reason that one of these strategies will be far more effective than the other. But so far, the line has held steady at Los Angeles -3.5 at sportsbooks, and the total has stuck at 48.5.

So, what is the potential betting impact of these travel strategies — both on this game and Week 2 for both teams?

We asked a bunch of oddsmakers — including one based in Australia — and handicappers for their thoughts.

It's always best to ask those with first-hand experience, so I reached out to Adam Hamilton, the head of racing and talent at Entain in Australia and New Zealand, for an on-the-ground report. While Hamilton noted the buzz surrounding the game in Melbourne and more money wagered on the Rams to cover, he was one of several oddsmakers in favor of the Rams' strategy.

"Fascinating difference in travel approach," Hamilton wrote in an email to Yahoo Sports. "Is the chance to acclimatize and settle [in] negated by the distractions and almost relaxing too much? While it's great for promotion of the game to have San Francisco here so early, I'd argue the Rams' approach is better. I love my horse racing and it's interesting most trainers would rather travel to a race interstate or overseas as close as possible."

Multiple oddsmakers that Yahoo Sports spoke with noted that the travel wouldn't have an impact on the spread or the way the public bet on it. One oddsmaker said he would've opened the game Rams -4.5 if it was being played at their true home in SoFi Stadium.

"I have been pretty in the weeds on circadian rhythms for a long time," Rob Pizzola, a sharp NFL handicapper and owner of The Hammer, told Yahoo Sports via text message. "I believe the Rams' plan is better because they are going to be playing on an optimal body clock. The 49ers will get acclimated to the facility and everything else a bit better, but they are going to end up on a morning body clock in Melbourne."

Several other oddsmakers theorized that San Francisco's approach was better, in terms of being able to adjust to the time, knowing their surroundings, ability to treat injuries on the ground, etc.

Perhaps one longtime Vegas oddsmaker put it best: "My first thought is the Rams are nuts. But they had a similar strategy with a game in London and they played great. Short answer is I have no idea. Either way, I'm letting the action dictate the number."

An interesting point was raised by Dr. Cathy Anne Goldstein on Ed Feng's Power Rank podcast , though. She noted that it takes about a day per time zone crossed to fully adjust, which means that even though the 49ers were coming in a week early, they wouldn't be able to fully adjust to the time in Melbourne — needing over two weeks to do so.

"[The 49ers] are going to be partially misaligned and it's not just that internal circadian misalignment with the time in Melbourne," Dr. Goldstein said. "They're also going to have sleep deprivation and poor performance while they're training and trying to recover and optimize for themselves for the game. So I think this is not a good strategy."

With the game at 10:35 a.m. local time — which translates to 5:35 p.m. the previous day in Los Angeles or San Francisco — being partially misaligned could be an even bigger disadvantage than flying in, playing and flying out. Yahoo Sports' own Jeff Eisenberg did a deeper dive on the science behind it all in this article earlier this week .

"What the Rams are doing — their body clock is going to remained aligned to L.A. time, leading up to the game they'll be sleeping normally and training normally," Dr. Goldstein added. "I personally think this is a much better strategy to address this massive change in time zones."

Thomas Gable, sportsbook director at The Borgata in Atlantic City, added, "I asked some Australian oddsmakers and they all believe the Rams are making a big mistake in [their travel plan]. I would tend to favor the under in this game, and they're of that belief as well."

What is the impact for both teams in Week 2?

Assuming the game doesn't end in a tie, the differing travel strategies will also have an impact on the rest of the season — especially in Week 2. The 49ers return to play three straight home games (-12.5 vs. Miami Dolphins , -10.5 vs. Arizona Cardinals , -2.5 vs. Denver Broncos ) and won't have to leave the West Coast again until a Week 7 game at Atlanta .

The Rams host the New York Giants in Week 2 as 9.5-point favorites, followed by consecutive road trips to Denver and Philadelphia and a home game against the Buffalo Bills . Los Angeles' schedule is far less forgiving, but the Rams may have an advantage in Week 2 by never adjusting to the Melbourne time zone.

"Maybe they're thinking ahead to Week 2, if we're not changing the body clocks then it's less of an effect," Gable added. "I believe there's going to be more of an effort to fade both of these teams in Week 2 than necessarily what happens in this week."

Either way, one team is going to end up 0-1 with a long trip back to the West Coast, and the other will likely be touting its travel plans as a big reason for a Week 1 victory.

articles.title: Drake Maye, Patriots on Wrong Side of NFL History with Ultra Rare Stat in Loss to Lock, Seahawks
articles.summary: The New England Patriots earned a dubious distinction in their 13-10 road loss to the Seattle Seahawks to open the 2026 NFL regular season on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots earned a dubious distinction in their 13-10 road loss to the Seattle Seahawks to open the 2026 NFL regular season on Wednesday night.

According to OptaSTATS , the Pats became the first NFL team in the past 30 years to throw three or more interceptions, take three or more sacks, commit three or more penalties and score no points in a single quarter:

New England entered the fourth quarter with a 10-3 lead and seemed to be in firm control, as Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold left the game after the opening offensive series of the contest due to a hip injury and was replaced by Drew Lock.

Despite that, Seattle mounted a comeback, tying the game in the fourth quarter on a 45-yard touchdown pass from Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and then taking the lead on a Jason Myers field goal with 5:50 remaining.

Both of the Seahawks' scores in the fourth quarter came on the back of interceptions thrown by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, but Maye had a chance to redeem himself on New England's final drive.

Maye got the Pats as close as Seattle's 16-yard line, but disaster struck for New England on a third-and-5, as Maye was flushed from the pocket and made an ill-advised throw.

Rather than throwing the ball away, taking the field goal and likely going to overtime, Maye attempted to hit Mack Hollins in the end zone, only for Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe to reel in the game-winning interception.

That marked Maye's third interception of the game and the quarter, and it ended the season opener in heartbreaking fashion for the Patriots.

Much like during the Patriots' 29-13 loss to the Seahawks in the Super Bowl last season, New England struggled mightily on offense on Wednesday, creating at least some concern regarding how they will handle the stout defenses of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars the next two weeks.

Perhaps even more concerning is the status of Patriots star wide receiver AJ Brown, who went down with an ankle injury in the third quarter and did not return.

articles.title: Shawne Merriman says Rams' Aaron Donald-Myles Garrett combo is 'insane' for NFL offenses: 'Pick your poison'
articles.summary: Shawne Merriman said the Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett pairing on the Los Angeles Rams creates an impossible "pick-your-poison" nightmare for offenses.
articles.body: Whenever a new season begins in any sport, it’s usually the team that won the previous year’s championship that has the biggest target on their backs. For the 2026 NFL season, it doesn’t seem to be the Seattle Seahawks, but rather the team they beat in the NFC Championship Game to reach the Super Bowl: the Los Angeles Rams. Super teams are hard to come by when 53 men are stacked onto a roster, but the Rams have come pretty close entering the new campaign, with the reigning MVP Matthew Stafford leading the way on a high-powered offense, while LA revamped its defense with a pair of Defensive Players of the Year on the defense live. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE And one of them came out of retirement just to take another crack at winning another Super Bowl ring. Aaron Donald, the 10-time Pro Bowl and eight-time First team All-Pro defensive tackle, officially ended his days outside football by rejoining the team he helped to win a Super Bowl in 2021. He joins Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and new single-season sack record holder, whom the Rams acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Cleveland Browns this offseason. If the Rams weren’t scary enough when Stafford & Co. have the ball in their hands, this combo strikes fear into the eyes of their opponents just by being on the schedule each week. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The expectations and potential of what this combo could do to offenses in 2026 has got football players, coaches and fans in a collective whirlwind. And one former NFL star linebacker thinks the hype couldn’t be more real. "Just insane. I mean, it’s insane because every week will be a pick-your-poison situation," Shawne Merriman, All-Pro linebacker for the San Diego Chargers and Buffalo Bills, told OutKick in a recent interview. "Who do you want to focus on? Because the other one is going to make plays." "Me being in my situation when I played, I knew I was going to get a lot of slide protection and chips off the edge and things like that. But you can’t do it to both sides. They have enough playmakers that, if you leave those guys one-on-one, it’s going to be damaging." To Merriman’s point, offensive lines will have to choose who they wish to focus on when the ball is snapped. It’s nearly impossible to be able to pick up Garrett and Donald with 1-on-1 matchups at the line without getting beat and potentially blowing up the play. There’s a reason the term "game wrecker" is used for certain players, and it’s been used time and time again for both Donald and Garrett throughout their respective careers. For Garrett especially, Merriman thinks joining the Rams will unlock an extra gear fans might not believe they’d ever see. "I want to add that people don’t understand, I give a lot of credit to our offense on my career because we were able to score so many points," he explained. "I mean, Phil [Rivers], L.T. [LaDainian Tomlinson], [Antonio] Gates, we knew we were putting up points every game. So, what happens is, you pin your ears back and go when the score gets 14-3, or 17-6. You can pin your ears back and go as a pass rusher. "Well, Myles Garrett, he never had that situation in Cleveland. He never had it with these guys in a decisive win, or teams had to throw the ball a lot because obviously you don’t want to throw the ball as much when Myles Garrett is sitting on the side. So, that’s the scary part. Now, he can just go because those games can get out of hand." As for Donald, Merriman was very confident in saying that he is "still a top three player at 80% of what he is," which is what many have been echoing. As a defensive tackle, Donald was able to do things nobody at the position did on a consistent basis: get to the quarterback. He led the league in sacks in 2018 with 20.5, while totaling 111 over his future Hall of Fame career. REIGNING MVP MATTHEW STAFFORD LOCKS IN EXTENSION WITH RAMS WORTH UP TO $60M WITH INCENTIVES He may have set that Hall of Fame clock back a few years by returning, but at 35 years old, Donald is still one of the craftiest, strongest, and elusive defensive tackles the NFL has ever seen. Merriman expects him to prove why he’s one of the greats in 2026. "If he comes back and he’s the same player – I’m sure it’s going to take some time to get used to football movements and get going again. But Aaron Donald is still a top three player at 80% in the NFL, which is scary," he said. "You can’t comprehend what that looks like. We haven’t seen anything like this before, because Myles Garrett in his own right can go down as the best pass rusher of all time, at least at the defensive end position. I love Bruce Smith, he’s one of my favorite players. I wore No. 56 because of Lawrence Taylor, but before this thing is all said and done, [Garrett] can go down as the best on his own. And you gotta put Aaron Donald down as the one or two best D-tackles of all time." Of course, all of this is being said before the Rams even kick off in Melbourne tonight at 8:35 p.m. ET, where Donald won’t be playing with L.A. wanting to give him more time to ramp up before taking the field once again. But the Rams are pegged as a team that embodies the "Super Bowl or bust" mantra this season. "Football is a finnicky sport, man. There’s been some ‘super teams’ in the past where it’s big names on paper and things just don’t go their way," Merriman said. "But how they’re built and constructed, on both sides of the football by the way, it’s hard not to believe they end up, at the bare minimum, back in the NFC Championship Game this year."

articles.title: Sam Darnold injury update: Seahawks learn key detail after quarterback is forced out early in season opener
articles.summary: NFL News: Sam Darnold’s night ended almost as quickly as it began, leaving the Seattle Seahawks with an immediate concern on the opening night of the NFL season.
articles.body: Sam Darnold’s night ended almost as quickly as it began, leaving the Seattle Seahawks with an immediate concern on the opening night of the NFL season. The quarterback was forced out after suffering a hip injury on the first drive, but early testing has given the defending champions reason for some optimism. Darnold avoided a fracture, although the Seahawks are still waiting for a more detailed medical assessment.Sam Darnold Injury Update Brings Encouraging NewsThe Seahawks had little time to settle into their season opener before their plans changed. Darnold left the game after the early injury and was taken to Harborview Medical Center in Seattle for further evaluation.The first major update came from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, who reported that a CT scan did not provide a final diagnosis but offered an encouraging sign. Darnold is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Thursday, which should give Seattle a much clearer picture of the injury and how long he could be unavailable."Sources: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold has been at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle, undergoing a CT scan on his hip. The initial test was encouraging but inconclusive, and Darnold now is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Thursday."For Seattle, the most important piece of news so far is that the initial tests did not show a hip fracture. A serious fracture could have kept Darnold out for a large part of the season and forced the Seahawks to reshape their plans at quarterback.Head coach Mike Macdonald also sounded positive when discussing the situation after the game."Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the team got good news on Sam Darnold, who underwent tests that ruled out a hip fracture. Still more tests to come. But Macdonald sounded upbeat about the initial prognosis."That update does not mean Darnold is ready to return. The MRI remains an important next step, particularly because the Seahawks need to know whether there is damage that could limit his mobility or keep him sidelined for several weeks.Seahawks Quarterback Situation Ahead of Week 2While Darnold’s status remains uncertain, Seattle has already shown that it can compete without its starting quarterback. Drew Lock stepped in and helped the Seahawks rally to a 13-10 victory over the New England Patriots.That result could prove especially valuable if Darnold needs time away from the field. Lock has experience in Seattle and now has an early opportunity to keep the offense moving while the team waits for a definitive diagnosis.The Seahawks are scheduled to face the Arizona Cardinals on the road next week. Whether Darnold can take part will likely depend on Thursday’s MRI results and how he responds during practice.For now, Seattle can take some comfort from the news that a fracture has been ruled out.
