The Boston Bruins hit the links yesterday and will exchange their clubs for sticks for today's captains' practice.

The regular season is 19 days away, and the Bruins still do not have a captain. Marco Sturm provided an update, though not much of one, at yesterday's golf outing, and Elias Lindholm spoke on the existing leadership group.

Elsewhere around the league, a Massachusetts native wants to come back east. Chris Kreider and the Ducks mutually agreed to terminate his contract, and the Boxford native (and his $6.5M cap hit) now sits on waivers. The Oilers signed one of the five players acquitted in the 2018 Hockey Canada sexual assault case, and the Red Wings may have a GM by default. Two Sportsnet analysts re-upped, and the 2027 NHL Draft will look the same as the last two years.

The hockey world is also mourning the loss of player, coach, and longtime ESPN analyst Barry Melrose, who passed away Wednesday at 70.

Happy Thursday, catch up on Bruins and league news in today's Daily Bean :

STURM/CAPTAIN : The Boston Bruins Foundation hosted its 23rd annual golf tournament yesterday at The Pinehills in Plymouth. Bruins of the past and present gathered for a round on the course, but Marco Sturm said the team is still "in the process" of naming the 28th captain in franchise history.

CAPTAINS' PRACTICE : The Bruins will be back at Warrior Ice Arena this morning. The last captains' practice starts at 10:00 AM.

The Bruins will open rookie camp on Friday at Warrior. On Saturday, the rookies will travel to Buffalo for games on Sunday and Monday.

Hockey Hall of Fame (via 𝕏) : Patrice Bergeron 's banner is now up at the Hockey Hall of Fame.

Sportsnet : Chris Kreider and the Ducks are terminating his contract. The Anaheim Ducks placed the Boxford, MA, native on waivers yesterday after mutually agreeing to a contract termination. Elliotte Friedman reported that the 35-year-old left winger has a preference to play in the East, "closer to family." He also will not report if he's claimed somewhere he does not want to play.

Immediately, eyes shifted toward the black and gold.

Sportsnet : The Edmonton Oilers signed forward Alex Formenton yesterday. Formenton was one of five players acquitted in the sexual assault trial involving Canada's 2018 World Juniors team. He has not played in the NHL since the 2021-22 NHL season and posted 23 points (13-10–23) last year with Ambri-Piotta in the Swiss league.

Detroit Hockey Now : The Red Wings are the only team in the NHL without a GM. At Tuesday's virtual meeting with NHL GMs and head coaches, AGM Shawn Horcoff represented the Red Wings. DHN dug, but could not find anyone from another NHL club who is gearing up to make the move. Is Shawn Horcoff going to be the GM by default?

TSN : The 2027 NHL Draft will once again be decentralized. This will mark the third straight decentralized draft, with all 32 teams and staff remaining in their home cities. The draft is set for June 25-26.

ESPN : Barry Melrose, a former player, coach, and beloved hockey analyst, passed away at 70. Melrose coached Wayne Gretzky and the LA Kings in the 1990s. He worked at ESPN from 1996 until 2023 and retired after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Tributes poured in from Melrose's ESPN colleagues , among many more around the NHL.

articles.title: Drake Maye gets dragged through the mud by NFL fans after horrific game, troubling trend
articles.summary: Drake Maye threw three interceptions as the New England Patriots blew a 10-point lead to Drew Lock and the Seahawks in the NFL season opener.
articles.body: The more things change, the more they stay the same. For Drake Maye, that's not a good thing. The New England Patriots gave up a 10-point lead to Drew Lock and the Seattle Seahawks in Wednesday night's NFL opener, and their star quarterback was, once again, a problem. A big one. DRAKE MAYE'S TERRIBLE DECISION GIFTS SEAHAWKS OPENING NIGHT WIN AS PATRIOTS LEFT STUNNED TO START NFL SEASON Maye, coming off a postseason in which he turned it over eight times in four games, threw three more interceptions Wednesday night, including one of the worst picks you'll ever see on what ended up being the final, back-breaking play of the night for New England. Lordy. I've watched it a dozen times, and it gets worse each time I press play. Just brutal on so many levels. Anyone watching the game could smell that one coming, by the way. Maye couldn't connect on a pass down the field all night long, with almost every completion coming at the line of scrimmage. New England's gameplan was shockingly basic: force-feed Rhamondre Stevenson 18 times for 2.7 yards a carry, and then throw it to ... Rhamondre Stevenson ... in the flat for a gain of 3. That was it. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's become a familiar sight for football fans, dating back to last season's suspect postseason run — after a regular season that was equally suspect given the Pats played one of the easiest schedules in the league. It's Year 3 for Maye, and, clearly, fans are starting to notice a trend: Tough to argue with those Drake Maye stats I could go on and on. NFL Twitter is a hellscape when you throw up an egg like that. It doesn't help that this was the season opener and fans had eight months of hot takes to get off their chests. I get it. It's what makes this sport the best in the world. Boston fans love their quarterbacks. They've been begging Drake Maye to be a Tom Brady replacement for three years now. They'll defend him to their last breath. But last night was completely indefensible. Maye went 1 of 6 on throws 15+ yards down the field, with three interceptions. That's almost impossible to do as an NFL quarterback — especially one who fans argued should've beaten out Matt Stafford for MVP last season. The Patriots could never get it going on offense. Maye brutally underthrew A.J. Brown on a flea-flicker in the second quarter — Brown would later get hurt — and the team somehow blew a 10-0 lead to DREW LOCK in the fourth quarter. The internet was ready to pounce, and Maye served them up a fastball right over the middle. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Obviously, it's just one game. The first game of the season is always weird, by the way. Odd things will happen this weekend that you won't see for the rest of the year. Trust me. But, unlike last season, the schedule doesn't get any easier for Maye and the Patriots. They get the Steelers, Jags and then Bills over the next three weeks. Maye will probably be fine. But this one is worth monitoring.

articles.title: ‘You can’t throw three interceptions’: Mike Vrabel reacts to Drake Maye performance
articles.summary: The New England Patriots fell to the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night in what was a very winnable game, with Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold going out wi...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots fell to the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night in what was a very winnable game, with Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold going out with an injury on the first drive of the game. However, some second-half interceptions doomed the Patriots.

After the game, Vrabel did not shy away from the fact that Drake Maye 's picks ultimately cost his team the game.

With the Patriots holding a 10-3 lead late in the third quarter and moving into Seahawks territory, Maye tossed his first interception of the game on a deep throw. Seattle capitalized on the turnover, turning the possession into a touchdown.

On the ensuing possession, Maye was picked off again on a third-and-long, giving the Seahawks the ball in Patriots territory. Seattle once again took advantage, converting the turnover into a field goal to grab a 13-10 lead.

Then, on the Patriots' final offensive drive of the game, Maye threw his third interception while attempting to force a pass into the end zone on third down. The turnover ultimately denied New England an opportunity to attempt a game-tying field goal with only seconds remaining.

In the end, all three of the Patriots' final possessions resulted in interceptions by Maye.

"I lost patience, and it cost us. Decisions that cost us the game on my part… You can't have those. It's unacceptable. I gotta get back to work, because that wasn't how I play football," Maye said after the game.

After the game, Vrabel offered his candid thoughts on his quarterback's performance as he did not shy away from the fact that Maye's turnovers were the difference in the game.

"You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that," Vrabel said after the game during his postgame press conference.

With those three turnovers, the Patriots lost the turnover battle 3-0. Vrabel knows that it's difficult to win a game when that happens.

"We can't turn the ball over and we have to create more turnovers," Vrabel said. "There's a few things we have to eliminate that get you beat in this league."

That said, Vrabel still has confidence in his young quarterback as he has made the decision to stick by him despite the interceptions.

"It's a long season. Gotta hold your head up high," Vrabel said of Maye. "We have nothing but the utmost confidence in him."

articles.title: 3 bold predictions for the New York Jets 2026 offense
articles.summary: Here are Jets Wire's 3 bold predictions for the team's offense in 2026.
articles.body:
The New York Jets are getting ready for the start of the regular season when they open the season in Tennessee to face their former head coach Robert Saleh and the Titans. The expectations are high for this Jets team and plenty is at stake in head coach Aaron Glenn's second season at the helm.

General manager Darren Mougey has added plenty of new weapons for quarterback Geno Smith , including first-round rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. Mougey also made sure to keep an important piece of the offense in the fold, giving running back Breece Hall a three-year extension .

The pieces are definitely in place and on paper, the offense has potential to be much better compared to last season. But, we won't know for certain until the games are played.

With that, here are Jets Wire's hree bold predictions for the offense in 2026:

Geno Smith will throw for over 4,000 yards

Smith is eager to prove that his only season with the Raiders was nothing more than an aberration. He looked good in camp and was impressive in his only offensive drive of the preseason, completing all seven passes and a touchdown against Pittsburgh 's first-string defense. His supporting cast this year with the Jets is ten times better than what he had last season in Vegas, including Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell , who had a strong rapport with Smith throughout training camp.

The Jets won't be an elite team in 2026 and I would expect them to play from behind in quite a few games this season. Last year, that would have have been a death sentence with Justin Fields and Brady Cook at quarterback. Smith is a competent quarterback and will look to redeem himself after his first run with the Jets was a failure. With the talent assembled for him on offense, Smith will become the first Jets quarterback to hit 4,000 passing yards in a season since Joe Namath did it in 1967.

Breece Hall will have over 2,000 Yards From Scrimmage

Hall signed a three-year contract extension to stay with the Jets probably because he was excited about his role in Frank Reich's offense. Last year, the Jets didn't utilize Hall much as a pass catcher, probably because they didn't have a quarterback who could get him the ball consistently.

He's the ultimately dual threat and you can bet Reich will have some tricks up his sleeve to maximize Hall's production. Despite the team's terrible 2025 season, Hall still managed to rush for over 1,000 yards, which is incredible to say the least. Outside of Dylan Parham replacing John Simpson, the rest of the offensive line returns and he finally has a quarterback who can get him the ball in Smith. 2026 could be the season we finally talk about Hall among the best running backs in the league.

Taylor and Sadiq combine for 1,000 yards and 8 touchdowns

It's tough to recall the last offensive coordinator that featured the tight end in their game plan. Probably not since Dustin Keller during the Rex Ryan era. Selected in the second round of the 2025 draft, Mason Taylor was on his way to a solid rookie season before a neck injury cost him the last four games. He's fully healthy and was utilized in the preseason with the first-team offense, which is a good sign for his role in the offense.

The Jets drafted Sadiq with one of their three first-round picks and while he's listed as a tight end, he can also be lined up in the slot thanks to his 4.36 speed and his size (6'3", 241 lbs.). Taylor and Sadiq have potential to be x-factors in this offense and excellent security blankets for Smith when he needs to quickly get rid of the ball. They can be dangerous weapons in the red-zone and can take pressure off of Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the passing game, allowing both more scoring opportunities. It's refreshing to see the Jets finally incorporate the tight end in the offense. It's even more refreshing that they now have two who will make an impact on game day.

articles.title: 30 most important Bills players of 2026: No. 5 Dion Dawkins

articles.body:
As the Buffalo Bills prepare for the 2026 NFL season, Bills Wire will take a look at the most important contributors on their roster. The team has some cornerstone players who will be returning for another shot at bringing a Lombardi Trophy to Buffalo, and they'll have help from some new additions as well.

Leading up to the season, we will be counting down the top-30 most important players on the roster. We'll recap their 2025 season, look ahead to what they'll offer in 2026, and tackle the most pressing questions surrounding them this coming year.

Dion Dawkins missed just two games in 2025, one in Week 13 with a concussion and the other in Week 18 while the Bills rested starters. He made his fifth consecutive trip to the Pro Bowl. Pro Football Focus gave him a 74.1 overall grade for the year, which ranked 26th among NFL tackles. He ranked seventh among all tackles in pass blocking with a grade of 81.8.

Dawkins has 153 career starts (all for the Bills), with 16 of them coming in the postseason.

Dawkins returns as the starting left tackle for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. Dawkins reportedly lost 43 pounds in the offseason, focusing on becoming lighter and quicker as he enters his 32-year-old season.

"I will be quicker, faster and more lean on the football field," Dawkins said this summer on the Up & Adams Show. "Being in the offseason, being around Myles Garrett , I said 'you know what, this guy is the best for a reason.' He looks like the best. He acts like he's the best. He trains like he's the best. He works out like he's the best. He's the best. What does Dion do? Ok, I want to do everything the exact same way. On the football field, I'm going to be quicker."

Biggest question: How will new pieces fit together?

While Dawkins' role as the left tackle and the protector of Allen's blindside will remain the same, there will be a couple new faces around him. For one, he'll have a new running mate in Alec Anderson , who replaces David Edwards at left guard. And, the Bills also have a new offensive line coach in 2026 as Pat Meyer replaces the now-retired Aaron Kromer. This will be Dawkins' fourth o-line coach in his ten years as a pro. articles.title: One game doesn’t define a season, but Patriots loss to Seattle revealed plenty | Karen Guregian
articles.summary: In the big picture, the Patriots loss to Seattle doesn't mean much. But it was revealing nonetheless.
articles.body:
SEATTLE - Opening games don't make or break a season. They aren't necessarily the best barometer of how a season ultimately goes.

Last year, the Patriots lost the season opener and didn't look particularly good. A few games later, they ripped off 10 straight wins, and wound up in the Super Bowl.

The year before that, the Jerod Mayo-coached team upset Cincinnati on the road, looked like they might be a player in the AFC, and only won three more games the rest of the way.

What to make of Wednesday night's 13-10 season opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl 60 rematch?

Let's just say it was informational on many fronts. It revealed plenty.

Drake Maye shouldn't be anointed the savior just yet. After an MVP worthy campaign in 2025, there were heightened expectations for the Patriots quarterback in 2026, even after a disappointing postseason.

Being in the second-year of Josh McDaniels' offense, having more command at the line to audible out of bad plays, being armed with better receivers with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs , and a revamped offensive line, Maye figured to be even more deadly.

It just didn't happen Wednesday night in Seattle. After taking a 10-0 lead, Maye completely unraveled. Perhaps trying to do too much, trying to make things happen after losing Brown to an ankle injury, Maye made mistake after mistake.

He threw three picks on three fourth quarter possessions, the last coming after driving the Patriots down to the 16 yard line with 26 seconds to go and the potential game-winning score within his grasp, or, at worst, a game-tying field goal.

He lofted up a horrible pass in the right corner of the end zone intended for Mack Hollins . Instead, Josh Jobe picked it off and that was the ball game.

All three picks were on Maye, who was far from his MVP form in the second half, and far from being a finished product.

"I mean, you can't throw three interceptions," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said immediately following the loss. "Drake knows that."

Maye tried to make sense of his poor play, but it still didn't sit well. He took accountability at the podium, and then sat at his locker for quite a while with his head down. Tommy DeVito did his best to lend support, but that didn't seem to work.

"(I) lost patience and it cost us, decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end," Maye said. "I vow to myself to be better and realize it's a long season but at the same time we can't have those. We can't have those.

"It's unacceptable and I know we got to get back to work. That wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots."

If anyone thought trading Kayshon Boutte wasn't a mistake, think again.

When A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury in the third quarter, one that kept him out of the rest of the game, and may very well keep him out awhile, having an insurance policy like Boutte probably would have been a godsend.

While Mack Hollins (4 catches, 51 yards) helped pick up some of the slack on the outside, Kyle Williams (0 catches, 0 targets) did zip. Ditto Romeo Doubs (0 catches, 3 targets), who had a critical fourth-quarter drop.

Doubs had looked so good the final weeks of camp, and during joint practices only to wilt in the game.

There's no guarantee Boutte would have been better, but it's hard to believe he wouldn't have been given his chemistry with Maye.

Instead, the Patriots opted to trade him to Houston for a backup safety ( Jaylen Reed ), and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick.

The offensive line, while improved, still wasn't good enough.

The Patriots couldn't run the ball at all in the first half. Rhamondre Stevenson averaged 2.8 yards per carry. Maye proved their best runner with 47 yards on seven carries. That doesn't bode well.

Alijah Vera-Tucker, a bit of a gamble given his injury history, is an All-Pro guard when he plays.

He didn't look like an All-Pro guard Wednesday night.

Will Campbell , after a forgettable Super Bowl, was better. But he had several costly penalties.

Holding the Seahawks to 13 points was terrific.

Newcomer Dre'Mont Jones played well on the edge, rookie Gabe Jacas made several plays that were encouraging, and Christian Gonzalez , who is now the proud owner of the NFL's top cornerback contract, had two pass breakups when he marked Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

The problem was he wasn't asked to mark him enough.

Ultimately, they still lost to a backup quarterback. Drew Lock took over after Sam Darnold (hip) was lost in the first series of the game.

He beat the Patriots by hitting Smith-Njigba with a 45-yard touchdown pass - safety Craig Woodson had a chance to bring him down, but whiffed on the tackle - and later got them in range for the game-winning field goal.

The defending Super Bowl champions made plays with the game on the line. The Patriots didn't.

Their top players rose to the occasion. The Patriots top guns, highlighted by Maye, didn't.

"Yeah, we didn't win the football game in the 4th (quarter), you know what I mean, the 2nd half. And that's really when you have to win these games in this league," Vrabel said. "It's finding a way to make some plays in the second half in critical situations. We didn't do that.

"We can't turn the ball over, and we have to create more turnovers. Again, it's a broken record. But we gotta have a chance. We gotta be great in that situation."

Again, that doesn't mean they won't be before season's end. But for a team coming off a Super Bowl appearance, a team that made moves geared toward closing the gap with the Seahawks, it was disappointing.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes backed to lead Kansas City Chiefs resurgence as he makes return from injury
articles.summary: Andy Reid says Travis Kelce "acts like he's going to play forever" as the tight end prepares for his 14th season with the Kansas City Chiefs, who welcome Patrick Mahomes back from last year's season-ending injury; the Chiefs begin their campaign against the Denver Broncos on Monday night
articles.body:
The Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last year while seeing their streak of nine straight AFC West division titles and seven straight AFC Championship Game appearances come to an end.

Reid's side entered the 2025 campaign having won three of five Super Bowl trips in six years as one of football's greatest modern dynasties, missing out on a historic three-peat after losing to the Philadelphia Eagles at Super Bowl 59 in New Orleans.

A down year was capped by a season-ending injury to Mahomes in December that saw the quarterback require surgery on a torn ACL and LCL. He is now scheduled to make his return against the Denver Broncos on Monday night.

"He's doing great," Reid told Sky Sports this offseason. "He spent seven hours a day here the whole offseason. And just busted his tail to make sure, within reason, within what the doctor's restrictions were, that he would maximize everything. And he did that.

"They keep track of him and then they give him the goals. We have a physical therapist here, Julie, that sets a standard for him. And then he has to reach that and then she won't let him go past that."

Rightly or wrongly, Mahomes will be greeted by more questions than ever before in his glittering NFL career as he returns from his first major injury layoff and his worst statistical campaign since entering the league.

By his history-making standards the three-time Super Bowl MVP has piloted a declining offense over the past two seasons, but there remains zero doubt among teammates over the man leading their charge.

"Pat is the best quarterback in the league, ain't much more we need to say about Pat," Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones told Sky Sports.

Chiefs guard Trey Smith, who signed a four-year, $94m contract extension in July, is among those tasked with protecting Mahomes upon his return, starting with a second-ranked Denver Broncos defense that led the league with 68 sacks.

"The dude's awesome, he makes it easy," Smith told Sky Sports. "He's a field general out there. He's just creative, but he's able to extend plays so much. So understand that you have an egg timer in your head going off. You have to block the guys until the last whistle.

"It's great to have him back. He's definitely a team leader. From day one when I stepped in this building, it was evident that he's one of our top guys and the talent shows for itself.

"And obviously being able to have him back is going to help us move that much further. All the guys are doing that in this place, they're doing a phenomenal job as well, but really excited to have him back."

Reid pointed towards his team's traffic light system, and the freedom Mahomes' off-script, out-of-structure creativity grants him to stretch the boundaries. Once the string-puller to a tricky-brimming offense that re-wrote league-wide trends, Mahomes' return comes with hopes of Kansas City rediscovering their spark.

"It gives you an opportunity to open things up a little bit," said Reid. "Within reason. Still got to execute, and so there's some red lights there that you got to stop at, but it sure allows you to have a long, long green light.

"There's certain things you can't do. And I don't say can't very often, but there's just certain things that we can't have. But other than that, the green light means you can go. And then that yellow light, we extend it for you a little bit. So it might be cautious, but we're okay. We extend it."

Mahomes will have Travis Kelce at his disposal once more after the veteran tight end delayed retirement to sign a contract extension that would eventually become worth three years and $54.7m.

He may not quite pose the same game-dictating threat, but Kelce did lead all Chiefs with 851 receiving yards last season. After deliberation, he decided there was more football left in him.

"He acts like he's going to play forever," said Reid. "So I don't even think about it, I don't worry about it. We just go and I'm going to use him up.

"If it's his last year, he's going to get used up for this year. If it's two years, we'll use him up for both years because he works his tail off and does a great job."

Speaking on his podcast "New Heights", Kelce credited Mahomes' determination and frustration throughout his recovery as inspiration for his decision to play on, such is his desire to continue serving his quarterback.

The Chiefs wouldn't quite feel the same without him.

"87 is going to go in the raptures," said Jones. "Just the amount of success and the leadership he's brought to this team, the amount of the energy.

"This thing without Travis Kelce, I can't imagine it. Hopefully he'll go back for another year. Hopefully this isn't his last.

"Yeah we got to bring Kelce back. That's the guy. He's the soul of the team."

The Chiefs strengthened on offense in free agency this year by signing running back Kenneth Walker III in the wake of his Super Bowl-winning campaign with the Seattle Seahawks. They meanwhile re-signed veteran corner L'Jarius Sneed and spent the sixth overall pick on LSU corner Mansoor Delane, their highest draft pick since selecting Mahomes 10th overall in 2017.

Reid's side won't forget the shortcomings of last season, but insist they will not dwell on them in a league capable of turning the tide in a flash.

"Its definitely frustrating," Smith added. "We didn't reach any of our goals. As long as I've been here we've always been doing AFC Championship or better, so obviously falling short it's not a good feeling. It left a bad taste in our mouths. And something that we have to address and just be better from.

"You're going to get challenged. Going to AFC Championship or better every single year is not normal. It's the NFL, so you had an NFL moment, but you can learn a lot from your losses. Feelings you have, you know, don't forget that, and you obviously don't want to experience that again."

The Chiefs surrendered their monopoly on the AFC West last season as Sean Payton and Bo Nix's Broncos produced a 14-3 record on their way to clinching the No 1 seed in the conference. Kansas City's 6-11 record marked their worst since going 2-14 in 2012.

"Sometimes you have your ups and downs, but you're able to learn a lot through it," said Jones. "I think we learned a lot last year. It didn't go the way we planned it. But I think it was a wake-up call to not only players, but organisation. And we've got a lot of young talent here.

"Different teams, same expectations. Win the AFC West, have the playoff games at home, and then make it to the Super Bowl. So I think those is that order right there. And it starts with Monday night against Denver."

articles.title: Is Jason Kelce quietly turning New Heights podcast into NFL’s next Pat McAfee Show?
articles.summary: NFL News: Jason Kelce may be taking his personal New Heights podcast into progressively serious NFL territory.The podcast he hosts with his younger brother, Tra.
articles.body: Jason Kelce may be taking his personal New Heights podcast into progressively serious NFL territory.The podcast he hosts with his younger brother, Travis Kelce, has built its identity around football, family, humor, and the type of behind-the-scenes conversations that traditional sports broadcasts can never replicate.But a recent discussion about Patrick Mahomes’ injury return report has raised a challenging question: Is Jason gradually transforming New Heights from a light-hearted family entertainment podcast into a major NFL media platform?During the conversation, Jason highlighted Mahomes’ return from the knee injuries he suffered in December 2025 and confidently declared that the Kansas City Chiefs ace quarterback would be on the gridiron. He then asked Travis whether he had seen Mahomes’ trademark mobility during practice.Travis, though, intentionally avoided sharing specific practice details. He instead turned to Kenneth Walker in a Chiefs jersey. That distinction is crucial.Jason was not delivering an official NFL injury report.He was using the New Heights podcast to discuss one of the league’s most popular stories with someone who has firsthand access to Mahomes. Is that breaking too many barriers? Extremely thin line there!Jason Kelce’s Patrick Mahomes injury update at New HeightsPatrick Mahomes’ return is inevitably a blockbuster point of discussion. He suffered ACL and LCL injuries in December 2025 and has spent the offseason rigorously working toward a Week 1 comeback.Nevertheless, Jason’s wording on the New Heights podcast was reportedly stronger than the team’s official public language.Jason said Mahomes “will be out there,” but Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has used more cautious language, saying Mahomes was “most likely” to start Week 1 while leaving ample room for a suspected setback to change that positive outlook.Now that perhaps makes Jason’s comments better described as confident analysis and insider discussion, rather than breaking news.And that may in reality be the strength of New Heights. Jason may not need to compete directly with traditional NFL reporters. His advantage is probably direct access to Travis and an understanding of what life inside an NFL locker room really looks like.The comparison to Pat McAfee, however, is impossible to ignore.Jason Kelce vs Pat McAfeePat McAfee built a highly successful sports-media brand around personality, player access, news, interviews, humor, and strong opinions.Jason appears to be exploring some of the same territory, although there is no evidence that he is deliberately trying to copy-paste or walk the same path as McAfee.There is also no evidence that Jason is using New Heights to secure another broadcasting contract. He already has a major ESPN role, including NFL studio and game assignments.The more reasonable interpretation is that Jason understands the commercial power of his voice.He has the credibility of a former NFL player, the reach of New Heights, and an active NFL player sitting beside him every week to reportedly give him insider information.Is Jason Kelce overreaching with New Heights podcast?Maybe not yet. If anything, the Patrick Mahomes’ injury conversation just shows how the New Heights podcast can occupy an uncommon space between entertainment and sports journalism.Jason asks questions a traditional broadcaster might, and Travis offers the perspective of someone inside the Kansas City Chiefs’ locker room. So, again, there comes the thin line!Instead of appearing “overreaching”, the New Heights podcast seems to be evolving into something potentially more valuable:a personality-driven NFL media brand that can discuss major football news without abandoning the humor and family chemistry that made it successful in the first place.It has the much-coveted “personal” factor/angle.As for Jason sounding like McAfee? Jason Kelce may never become Pat McAfee - and there is no evidence that he wants to.But if New Heights continues blending insider access, NFL analysis, and entertainment, the comparison will eventually become impossible to ignore.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cowboys' Schottenheimer Talks George Pickens' Role, Changes to Offense for 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Coming off the best season of his career in 2025, the Dallas Cowboys want to keep opposing defenses on their toes by changing some of the ways they use George Pickens.
articles.body:
Coming off the best season of his career in 2025, the Dallas Cowboys want to keep opposing defenses on their toes by changing some of the ways they use George Pickens.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler they are intending to move Pickens all around rather than simply having him play the X position.

"He can play multiple spots," Schottenheimer said. "I know in Pittsburgh he got frustrated a little bit because he was always in one spot. He was always the X. We move him around a bunch. But the sky is the limit for GP."

Fowler also noted Schottenheimer explained he plans to "tweak" the Cowboys offense between 15 to 25 percent from what it was last season in an attempt "to keep sophisticated defenses guessing."

Per Pro Football Focus (h/t Mauricio Rodriguez of A to Z Sports), Pickens ranked 90th out of 91 receivers with at least 42 targets last season in percentage of snaps out of the slot (10 percent).

For perspective, Pickens was in the slot for 23 percent of his snaps during his final season with the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024.

One reason for Pickens' decrease in slot snaps is CeeDee Lamb is at his best playing from that spot, but he is more than capable when he lines up on the outside.

The benefit of having both Pickens and Lamb is few teams in the NFL can matchup with both of them. Dak Prescott is not afraid to throw a seam ball in the middle of the field.

Given how well Pickens controls his body and wins at the catch point, putting him in the middle of the field could open up more big plays for a Cowboys offense that ranked seventh in points scored last season.

Pickens will almost certainly welcome the chance for more potential easy targets as he looks to secure a long-term contract next offseason after receiving the franchise tag this year.

The 25-year-old finished 2025 with 93 receptions, 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He set career-highs in all three categories.

Schottenheimer will get to show off his new offense for the first time when the Cowboys open the 2026 regular season against the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin’s TV debut turns into a roast session after he fumbles three letters “JSN,” short for Jaxon Smith-Njigba
articles.summary: NFL News: Mike Tomlin has spent nearly two decades making NFL players sweat from the sidelines.He reportedly used to show intense frustration at them during pra.
articles.body: Mike Tomlin has spent nearly two decades making NFL players sweat from the sidelines.He reportedly used to show intense frustration at them during practices and games. Now the tables have turned. On his first night in the broadcast booth, it was three little letters that had him sweating, or at least inviting merciless roasting.The longtime Pittsburgh Steelers head coach made his broadcasting debut as an NBC analyst during the 2026 NFL season opener between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots.And before viewers could completely settle into Tomlin’s new career, he delivered an unforgettable moment.He simply couldn’t get “JSN” right. JSN is short for Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He is the star Super Bowl-winning wide receiver playing for the Seattle Seahawks.Maria Taylor corrects Mike Tomlin for misspelling Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s initialsWhile discussing Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Tomlin repeatedly referred to the star receiver as “JNS.”Not just one single harmless slip of the tongue. But repeated ones. That was when co-host Maria Taylor decided she had seen enough.“JSN. I’m not going to let you do it again. I’m not going to let you do it again. You said JNS!” Taylor told him, correcting the former head coach on live television.The head coach was caught off guard; he probably forgot what he was about to say. But he appreciated what Taylor did, saying, “Hey! I appreciate you taking care of me.”Taylor laughed it off and said, “Because usually this is the thing; coaches always talk in numbers. They’re not having to say names all the time. I got you, coach!”Mike Tomlin probably should know Jaxon Smith-NjigbaTomlin’s transition from coaching career to broadcasting career may take time. But he will definitely get there!Anyhow, cyberspace was not going to keep quiet about this tiny error. Especially since it’s someone who is hardly an obscure name in today’s NFL.The Seahawks wide receiver was coming off a monster 2025 campaign in which he led the league with 119 receptions, 1,793 receiving yards, and 10 touchdowns.He also earned first-team All-Pro honors and was named Offensive Player of the Year. To top it? He won the Super Bowl. And also secured a massive four-year, $168 million contract with an average annual salary of $42 million! The highest-paid wide receiver in NFL history at signing.So, yes, Tomlin probably should know who JSN is. And if he didn’t before kickoff, he certainly knows now! All thanks to Maria Taylor.Anyhow, the irony was almost too perfect. Tomlin spent years preparing players for the intricate details of football. Now, on his first massive broadcasting role, he was the one getting a lesson in basic nomenclature! How sad is that. Even if we forget, cyberspace will remember it forever.From Pittsburgh Steelers sideline executive to TV rookie analystMike Tomlin’s broadcasting transition was much-awaited, considering his brutally direct answers at press conferences and barked instructions from an NFL sideline.And when the transition came, he suddenly found himself under studio lights, expected to analyze the game while also navigating the unforgiving world of live television.There is no timeout in the broadcasting booth. There is no replay to erase an awkward sentence uttered in haste.And there is certainly no hiding when Maria Taylor catches you calling JSN “JNS” for the umpteenth time. She really did not want Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s name uttered wrong more than once!To Tomlin’s credit, he laughed off the correction and continued his analysis rather than letting the moment derail him, though he was derailed temporarily. But isn’t that how a veteran TV broadcaster roasts a rookie TV analyst? Maybe yes, maybe not! There’s a lot that the coach can take away from it… If not anything, then a warm welcome.The roast may be Mike Tomlin’s warm welcome to a TV careerThe “JNS” blunder may have ruthlessly stolen the spotlight, but it does not erase the football insight Mike Tomlin brought to the broadcast. He analyzed Smith-Njigba’s game and discussed the wide receiver’s exceptional movement and ability to get in and out of breaks.Still, cyberspace has already handed Tomlin his first viral broadcasting moment.After all those years of roasting Pittsburgh Steelers players from the sideline, Mike Tomlin finally got roasted himself!And the culprit? Not a blown coverage. Not a bad play call. Not even a fourth-down decision. Just three letters: J. S. N.Big warm welcome to television, Coach!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Suggests 'Certain People' with Packers Wouldn't Welcome Him Back in Retirement
articles.summary: Even after his playing career comes to an end, Aaron Rodgers isn't sure the Green Bay Packers will bring him back to Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
Even after his playing career comes to an end, Aaron Rodgers isn't sure the Green Bay Packers will bring him back to Lambeau Field.

Appearing on ESPN Milwaukee Radio's Wilde and Tausch show on Thursday (h/t ESPN's Rob Demovsky ), Rodgers suggested there are "certain people" currently working for the Packers who might not be keen to have him back in the building:

"I think there's some people that have a lot of affection for me, and I would assume we're talking four or five years from now that there will be fans who still have appreciation for what I've done, especially after so much time has passed. I think there's certain people in the building who wouldn't be totally on board, and maybe I wouldn't be on board if they were still there as well."

Rodgers didn't specifically mention anyone, but his relationship with Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst took a turn during the 2020 NFL draft when the team traded up to select Jordan Love with the No. 26 pick.

Even though there were fissures in the immediate aftermath of Love's selection, The Athletic's Matt Schneidman reported in May 2023 that it was "early" in the 2021 offseason that Rodgers' agent called Packers president Mark Murphy with a request to either fire Gutekunst or trade Rodgers coming off an MVP season.

Murphy retired from his position with the Packers in July 2025.

On the day of the first round of the 2021 NFL draft, Rodgers reportedly told Packers officials he wanted to be traded. They held firm in not moving him and remained together for two more seasons, with Rodgers winning another MVP award during the 2021 campaign.

Rodgers was traded to the New York Jets in April 2023, ending his 18-year tenure in Green Bay.

The Packers have some history with acrimonious quarterback breakups and repairing relationships. Brett Favre, who similarly watched the organization draft his successor when they took Rodgers in 2005, had a tumultuous dynamic with the club at the end before he was traded to the Jets in August 2008.

Things were eventually worked out between Favre and the Packers that he returned to Lambeau Field during the 2015 season to have his No. 4 jersey retired .

That was more than four years after Favre retired from the NFL. It remains to be seen if it would take Rodgers that long to get his No. 12 jersey retired, but it would seem almost certain to happen at some point given how important he is to the history of the franchise.

In the meantime, Rodgers will begin his 22nd NFL season on Sunday when he leads the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium.

articles.title: Breaking Down Rams, 49ers' Alternate Travel Approaches for NFL Week 1 Game in Australia
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers took two very distinct approaches to their long trip to Australia for their Week 1 opener.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers took two very distinct approaches to their long trip to Australia for their Week 1 opener.

The Niners were in Melbourne for nearly a week before the Rams touched down prior to Thursday's game.

San Francisco's players and staffers should have shaken off any jet lag well before the game kicks off. In the case of Los Angeles, the team might not be in Melbourne long enough for jet lag to be a factor.

The Rams tried to treat this like business as usual in terms of playing away from home.

"What gives me confidence is I'm not going to really make it a big deal," head coach Sean McVay told reporters . "It's, 'Hey, this is what the reality is. We've got a long way to go, but let's be ready to rock when that three-hour window that we're allotted comes.' That's what it is. To spend a bunch of time talking about it — I get it with you guys, too, like I understand your questions but for me, I've told you guys what our approach is. Our expectation is our guys will be ready to go and I'm not worried about it because I know what our plans are."

Anybody who has traveled abroad will testify to how difficult it can be to adjust after spending hours on a plane, which is compounded by the time change. Heading to Australia means crossing the international date line, in effect losing an entire day.

The accommodations for the Rams are obviously far better than what the typical traveler experiences, and that will have made it easier to get any needed sleep.

Still, their strategy for flying to Australia is going to be more of a storyline if Los Angeles comes out flat in Week 1.

articles.title: Week 1 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice on Top Fantasy Football Stars in Opening Games
articles.summary: Week 1 got underway on Wednesday night and will continue with Thursday's game between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers in Australia. However, fantasy managers will still have time to adjust the bulk of their lineups before Sunday's full slate.
articles.body:
Week 1 got underway on Wednesday night and will continue with Thursday's game between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers in Australia. However, fantasy managers will still have time to adjust the bulk of their lineups before Sunday's full slate.

The fantasy season is off and running, and it's time to pivot away from draft strategy toward in-season roster management. This can be a challenge in Week 1, as there is limited information and results with which to work. However, factors like past performances, projected roles, and individual matchups can help determine who to start and who to avoid.

You'll find recommendations for some of the league's top stars here. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The New Orleans Saints defense was surprisingly solid in 2025 and surrendered the seventh-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks. However, Jared Goff has been largely reliable at home and should have a full complement of pass-catchers with Sam LaPort trending in the right direction.

The Detroit Lions are looking to get off to a fast start with new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing and have traditionally been willing to run up the score when possible. This means Goff should have a solid floor and a very high ceiling in Week 1.

We're looking to avoid obvious must-starts like Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson in this exercise, but some other starts to consider include:

Sit: Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs

There's a very real chance that Patrick Mahomes will return from last year's torn ACL and reemerge as a strong fantasy starter. However, waiting to trust him would be advisable.

The Denver Broncos have a ferocious pass rush, and Mahomes isn't likely to trust his mobility right away coming off the injury. That could lead to more than a few dead plays and a lack of rushing upside.

The New York Giants should see some defensive improvements under new head coach John Harbaugh. However, it's likely going to take some time for the unit to fully blossom, and the departure of Dexter Lawrence does hurt.

Even with Lawrence in the lineup, the Giants surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing RBs in 2025. In his lone game against New York last season, Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams racked up six catches, 130 scrimmage yards, and a touchdown.

Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins is coming off a significant leg injury that ended his rookie season prematurely. That will likely impact his usage in a backfield that has a strong receiving back in Dylan Sampson.

The other concern here is that Judkins and the Browns will be on the road against a Jacksonville Jaguars defense that surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points (tied) to opposing running backs last season. The floor is simply too concerning to trust.

Another reason to like Goff is the fact that we should see a good amount of offensive back-and-forth between the Lions and the Saints on Sunday. Detroit had its fair share of defensive issues a year ago, and things aren't likely to be substantially better to start 2026.

This should lead to a big Week 1 for Saints receiver Chris Olave. He won't be sharing targets with rookie Jordyn Tyson, who is on IR, and he'll face a Lions defense that surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing receivers in 2025.

Michael Pittman Jr., Pittsburgh Steelers

2025 first-round pick Matthew Golden largely disappointed as a rookie, finishing with just 361 receiving yards and zero touchdowns. However, he is expected to see a bigger role in Year 2 following the departure of Romeo Doubs.

What sort of role Golden will possess remains to be seen, and managers should probably wait before thrusting Golden into their lineups. The Packers' Week 1 grudge match against the Minnesota Vikings will pit Golden against a defense that surrendered the fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers in 2025.

Kyle Pitts was a fairly reliable fantasy option last season but faces plenty of uncertainty heading into 2026. The Atlanta Falcons' quarterback situation leaves a lot to be desired, and Pitts will be in a brand new offense under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

The good news is that Stefanski's offense has traditionally featured his tight ends in the passing game. The Pittsburgh Steelers, meanwhile, surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing TEs in 2025.

Jake Ferguson has been a solid complementary option for the Cowboys over the past couple of seasons, but he may not see a significant role with Williams, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens all healthy.

Ferguson could also see a fair amount of rookie phenom Arvell Reese in coverage, and the Giants were actually pretty solid at limiting opposing tight ends last season. Their 2025 unit surrendered the ninth-fewest fantasy points to the position.

The first week of the 2026 NFL season is underway, and some managers may already find themselves in catch-up mode. Fortunately, there's still time to adjust lineups and seek help on the waiver wire before the bulk of the schedule unfolds on Sunday.

Here, you'll find an updated cheat sheet for the remainder of Week 1, a list of top value plays, and a few sleepers to consider plucking off the wire.

All rankings and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

Sleeper: Tyler Shough, QB, New Orleans Saints

We'd be a tad more bullish on New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough if rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson wasn't opening the season on injured reserve. However, Shough showed he can be a dynamic dual-threat down the stretch as a rookie and is a solid streaming option this season.

Shough will also get a favorable matchup out of the gate in 2026. The Detroit Lions will have a strong home-field advantage, but they surrendered the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing QBs a year ago.

Detroit's high-powered offense should also keep the Saints in a pass-heavy mode for much of the game. Shough should have a high floor, and his scrambling ability gives him an incredibly high ceiling.

The Louisville product is rostered in just 22.5 perc ent of season-long fantasy leagues and carries a budget-friendly value of $6.900 at FanDuel.

Sleeper: Mike Washington, Las Vegas Raiders

Las Vegas Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. would have intriguing sleeper value even if starter Ashton Jeanty wasn't dealing with an ankle sprain.

The Arkansas product showed during the preseason that his breakaway ability will translate to the NFL, and he figures to be a great complement to Jeanty. Remember, new offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak used a fairly balanced split between Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet as the Seattle Seahawks' OC.

Of course, Jeanty has been dealing with the ankle injury, and while he's expected to play in Week 1, he may not be close to 100 percent. Washington could have a big debut against a Miami Dolphins defense that surrendered the 12th-most fantasy points to RBs in 2025 before the roster was purged of veteran talent.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Danica Patrick over 2020 split as conflicting breakup stories spark a new controversy
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers has fired back at Danica Patrick over her comments about their 2020 breakup, strongly denying her version of their relationship. During .
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has fired back at Danica Patrick over her comments about their 2020 breakup, strongly denying her version of their relationship. During the September 10 episode of the “Not Just Football” podcast, Rodgers called the idea that he was a “monster partner” false and questioned why Patrick was still discussing their relationship years later. He also gave his own account of what led to their split.Aaron Rodgers responds to Danica Patrick’s emotional abuse claimsRodgers’ comments came after Patrick spoke about their relationship on “The Sage Steele Show” in May 2025. She described the relationship as “emotionally abusive” and said the breakup was the most painful experience of her life. Patrick also said Rodgers “leaves a trail of blood,” while explaining how badly the relationship affected her.Rodgers strongly pushed back on that account during his conversation with Pittsburgh Steelers teammate Cam Heyward. He said people only seem interested in the stories told by his former partners when his name is included.“So I’m this monster of a partner and it’s just fing horses,” Rodgers said. “Number one: Why are you still talking about me? It’s been years.”He then turned to his relationship with Patrick, saying she had recently retired from racing when they were together and, in his view, was struggling at the time.“I dated Danica. She had just retired. She was depressed and not fun to be around,” Rodgers said.Rodgers claimed he stayed because he wanted to support her and be a good partner. He said their relationship later changed, with “no intimacy” and little left between them.Aaron Rodgers and Danica Patrick’s breakup story differsRodgers also gave details about a house he was buying in Malibu. According to his account, Patrick asked whether they should buy it together. Rodgers said he declined, and the conversation made it clear to both of them that their relationship was heading toward an end.Patrick then suggested counseling, Rodgers said. The two went to counseling, but the situation became more difficult when the COVID-19 pandemic began and they were stuck together.That is very different from how Patrick later described the breakup. On “The Sage Steele Show,” she said the 2020 split felt sudden because her life had become closely tied to Rodgers. She said the relationship had damaged her confidence and left her emotionally drained.Rodgers said he was confused by Patrick’s later description of the breakup as being blindsided.“She tells a story that she was so blindsided and getting left by you, and that he leaves a trail of blood. And I’m like, what are you talking about? That’s not what happened,” he said.Rodgers and Patrick dated for about two years before ending their relationship in July 2020. After their split, Rodgers began dating actress Shailene Woodley. They became engaged in 2021, but later ended their relationship.Rodgers also mentioned another former girlfriend during the podcast without naming her. articles.summary: New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara, who suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain in his right knee during an Aug. 18 joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys, is reportedly about "two weeks" ahead of schedule, per Nick Underhill of New Orleans.Football, who expects the 10-year veteran to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions "barring a setback."
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara, who suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain in his right knee during an Aug. 18 joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys, is reportedly about "two weeks" ahead of schedule, per Nick Underhill of New Orleans.Football, who expects the 10-year veteran to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions "barring a setback."

Kamara is co-listed as a first-team running back with Travis Etienne, who signed a four-year, $47 million contract with New Orleans this offseason, on the Saints' unofficial depth chart .

That being said, one can expect the 27-year-old Etienne, who logged 1,399 yards from scrimmage and 13 touchdowns with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, to be the lead back.

From a fantasy standpoint, entering this season, the 31-year-old Kamara wasn't considered a top player. Per ESPN's point-per-reception rankings , Kamara was listed 49th among running backs and 142nd overall. He was even lower on FantasyPros (53rd among RBs, 158th overall).

Kamara, of course, used to be one of the greatest offensive weapons and fantasy producers in the NFL. From 2017-2021, Kamara averaged 1,500 yards and 13 touchdowns per season. He also caught 326 passes over his first four campaigns.

The former Tennessee Volunteer still remained productive from 2022-2024 with 1,347 yards on average and six touchdowns per year.

However, last year was a tough one for Kamara, who missed the final six games of the season with a Grade 2 MCL sprain. He finished the season with just a career-low 657 yards from scrimmage and one touchdown.

Naturally, one can have some pessimism about his 2026 season given how last year ended. From a fantasy standpoint, he's a bench option at best, and he's also available in 76 percent of Yahoo leagues right now.

That being said, Kamara clearly figures into the Saints' offensive plans, based on his depth chart placement.

Underhill also expressed optimism generally about Kamara.

"I think he's good to go," Underhill said.

"I think he's in good shape, and, you know, that's gonna open up the offense. It gives you the two-back looks that allows you to get people out to space. You can line up different ways, you can get in a different packages. If you don't have [Saints tight end Oscar Delp, who missed practice Wednesday], you can create some of that flexibility.

"I think, with two-RB stuff, I will be interested to see if they, I think Delp was going to kind of be a little bit of an H-back, so it'll be interesting to see if they put somebody else into that role just to kind of keep that open.

"But him being on the field helps. Obviously, [Etienne] is going to be RB1 this year, but I think AK is going to be a real weapon for them. Having him out there today just allows you to kind of start in a good place."

Kamara practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, so he's in good shape to play Sunday at this point. On the fantasy side, though, it's best to exercise caution and leave him on benches before we see how (and how much) the Saints utilize him this year.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin Shades Tua Tagovailoa Ahead of QB's Falcons Debut vs. Aaron Rodgers, Steelers
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and current NFL on NBC analyst Mike Tomlin isn't high on Tua Tagovailoa's prospects as quarterback of the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and current NFL on NBC analyst Mike Tomlin isn't high on Tua Tagovailoa's prospects as quarterback of the Atlanta Falcons.

While breaking down the upcoming game between the Steelers and Falcons in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season during Wednesday's NBC broadcast (h/t Chris Ward of SteelersNow.com), Tomlin was less than complimentary of Tua.

"It's less about [Steelers quarterback] Aaron [Rodgers] for me, and it's more about the quarterback on the other side. His last visit to Pittsburgh didn't go well. I was in the stadium that day. They lost. He got benched."

Tomlin was referencing the Steelers' 28-15 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 15 last season.

Tagovailoa threw for 253 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and he was sacked four times in the game. One week later, Miami benched Tua in favor of Quinn Ewers.

Originally the fifth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft by the Dolphins, Tagovailoa spent his first six seasons in Miami.

Results were mixed, as he went 44-32 as a starter, while throwing for 18,166 yards, 120 touchdowns and 59 interceptions over 78 games, but was unable to win a playoff game.

Tua also failed to take the Dolphins to the playoffs over his final two seasons in Miami, and he finished last season with just 2,660 yards, 20 touchdowns and 15 picks in 14 games.

The Dolphins cut ties with Tagovailoa and signed Malik Willis as his replacement this past offseason, opening the door for Tua to join the Falcons in free agency.

Atlanta needed a veteran quarterback following the departure of Kirk Cousins, and Tua was brought in to compete with Michael Penix Jr. for the starting job.

There was no true competition during training camp and the preseason, though, as Penix is still recovering from a torn ACL suffered last season, and did not appear in any preseason games.

Because of that, Tagovailoa was named Atlanta's starter essentially by default, although the decision was not officially made until this week.

Tagovailoa will have no shortage of high-end weapons at his disposal in the form of running back Bijan Robinson, wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts.

When the likes of Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle, De'Von Achane and Raheem Mostert were at their best in Miami, Tua played his best football, including a Pro Bowl campaign in 2023 that saw him lead the NFL with 4,624 passing yards, while also throwing 29 touchdown passes.

It is fair to wonder if Tagovailoa still has that level of play in him, but Tomlin seemingly doesn't expect to see it when the Falcons go on the road to face the Steelers on Sunday.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers roasts 'gutless' ESPN's integrity for its Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel coverage 'hypocrisy'
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers roasted ESPN for mostly ignoring the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel story while prominently featuring Jed York's arrest on its homepage.
articles.body: Most NFL quarterbacks have plenty on their proverbial plate this time of year and aren't too worried about the league's scandals or the coverage of those by the landscape's most dominant sports network ESPN. Not Aaron Rodgers. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is preparing for Sunday's season-opener against the Atlanta Falcons, but recently took time out to roast ESPN on the Not Just Football podcast with teammate Cam Heyward. On the show Rodgers criticized the network's coverage, or rather, the lack of coverage of what he called the "intimate relations" between New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and former ESPN and Athletic reporter Dianna Russini. "ESPN is really scared" of having him on the Pat McAfee Show to discuss that, Rodgers said. STEELERS DEFEND AARON RODGERS' RIGHT TO VOICE OPINIONS AFTER ESPN FAUCI SEGMENT Why? "Because I can speak up and speak my mind," he said. "And that McAfee thing rattled their feathers, because I didn't just say that on McAfee's show, who is, honestly, I love Pat, and he's done more for that network than any other horrible show they have on there that they think is they should pay those guys doing it. But I also said, you're a gutless organization. Because they haven't said anything. "They spend so much time on certain issues, but you won't talk one second about the Dianna Russini situation. What just happened? Uh, let's see, the owner of the Niners solicited a prostitute for [$160] in Ohio. That literally was the number one topic when you click on ESPN, right?" "They rotate the eight stories or whatever they have. But they usually have, like, the one story they feature. That was a featured story. So you bring in how many millions of eyes to that situation. Why do you want to throw Jed York under the bus? I don't know." 49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES Well, one side done, flip ESPN over to cook the other side, Aaron ... "But does that have the same effect as a reporter who, you know, has intimate relations with a coach?" Rodgers asked. "Who has a vote for MVP, who has a vote for Coach of the Year? "There was the thing about Morgan Moses going from the Jets to New England that was posted a day early. How many other inside stuff was shared? There are a lot of insiders out there. Do they all have strong integrity? I don't know. "But the fact that ESPN spent zero time on that story but Jed York gets popped ... and it's literally on the top of their roll ... That's hypocrisy." Rodgers critics have claimed he dabbles in conspiracy theories and however one feels about that, he's not afraid to discuss a conspiracy theory about ESPN's lack of Russini coverage. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "I think there's a lot more to it," he said. "The NFL is gonna protect the shield. And I respect that. But they're gonna do it by all means necessary." For the uninitiated, Russini and Vrabel were photographed at a Sedona, Arizona resort in April holding hands, embracing, spending time together at a pool and in a hot tub. Those photos and others pointing to a relationship beyond what is typical led The Athletic to conclude Russini's relationship with Vrabel was "in clear violation" of standards. That is a bad look for everyone involved. And ESPN, who employed Russini from 2015 to 2023, is wholly in bed with the NFL. The league owns a 10% stake of ESPN. "They got to be very very careful," Rodgers said. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Chris Johnson Writes Letter to His Kids on ALS Diagnosis, 'Biggest Reason I Keep Fighting'
articles.summary: Former NFL running back Chris Johnson penned a letter in The Players' Tribune to his children as he continues his fight with ALS.
articles.body:
Former NFL running back Chris Johnson penned a letter in The Players' Tribune to his children as he continues his fight with ALS.

He called his four kids "my biggest reason I keep fighting."

"All four of y'all, promise me you'll always stick together," Johnson said. "Love each other. Hold each other down. Life is going to change in ways none of us can predict, but don't ever let it change that.

"I believe in you guys. You each have unique talents and skills that you're gonna share with the world one day. I know it. I have big dreams for you. The same dreams that I think every father dreams about…… watching my kids graduate, walking my daughter down the aisle one day, seeing my boys become men, meeting my grandkids, and growing old with Brittany. And hopefully, God will make a way."

Johnson also recounted the process of his ALS diagnosis. He said he had been experiencing some weakness in his right arm, which prompted him to seek medical guidance. A doctor performed a nerve conduction study, and the eventual results pointed to the severity of his situation.

"I got on the plane and flew back home to you guys in Orlando, and I took a car straight to Honey Buns' school. That was the night of the play," he said. "The timing of it all was crazy. In my head I was so scared, but at the same time I still had to be your dad. When I saw Britt, we just kind of looked at each other. We took pictures that night, and looking back at them, you can just see the fear in both our eyes. I'll never forget sitting next to her in the auditorium just thinking about the unknown while Honey Buns was up on the stage."

Johnson first divulged his diagnosis in a June interview with Good Morning America 's Michael Strahan. He said he wanted to come forward so people can understand how quickly ALS can progress.

"Just over a year ago, I was picking up my 7-year-old daughter so she'd make a wish with her birthday cake," he told Strahan. "Today, I couldn't do that."

In his letter, Johnson credited his children with helping to maintain a sense of normalcy amid such difficult circumstances.

"Y'all are my biggest blessing," he said. "And right now, you know what part of that blessing I'm appreciating the most? I love that you still joke on me and mess with me, and laugh and smile and just act like everything is completely normal. Like everything's gonna be OK. It's crazy, in those small moments, I can forget everything else that's going on, because I swear it's like you don't even see ALS.

Johnson played 10 years in the NFL and was a three-time Pro Bowler. He's one of nine players who ran for 2,000 yards in a single season.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Tucker Kraft's 'Relatively Strong' Packers Contract Offer Ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: Tucker Kraft is entering the final year of his contract, but the Green Bay Packers have reportedly already made him a "strong offer."
articles.body:
Tucker Kraft is entering the final year of his contract, but the Green Bay Packers have reportedly already made him a "strong offer."

During an appearance Thursday on The Pat McAfee Show , ESPN's Adam Schefter reported, "The Packers have a relatively strong offer out there. … I don't know what the guarantee the Packers have to Tucker Kraft, but those conversations will go on up until the weekend."

Kraft's ceiling is to be one of the best tight ends in the league.

The 2023 third-round pick broke out in his second season in the league and tallied 50 catches for 707 yards and seven touchdowns, which seemed to set the stage for a monster 2025 campaign. And it started out that way, as he found the end zone six times in his first eight games.

However, the tight end tore his ACL and saw his season come to a premature end.

The torn ACL adds an element of risk to the contract discussions, as Kraft could need some time to return to form even though all indications are he will be ready to go for Sunday's season opener against the division-rival Minnesota Vikings.

But the ceiling surely outweighs the risk in the Packers' eyes.

Kraft is just 25 years old, has demonstrated notable chemistry with quarterback Jordan Love and was well on pace for double-digit touchdowns last season before the injury. In a perfect world for Green Bay, he will be a focal point of the aerial attack for the foreseeable future.

That will first require a new contract, but the team reportedly has that "strong offer" out there as the season opener approaches.

articles.title: Sam Darnold expected to miss Week 2, but may have avoided serious injury in win over Patriots
articles.summary: Sam Darnold was sacked and suffered a leg injury early in Wednesday's game.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks ' celebration over raising their Super Bowl banner and the start of a new season didn't last long Wednesday.

Quarterback Sam Darnold left the opening game against the New England Patriots after one series due to a hip injury. After undergoing tests on Thursday, he is expected to be ruled out for Week 2, per NFL Network, but — thanks to the Seahawks playing Wednesday — has much longer than usual to recover before Week 3.

Darnold was replaced by Drew Lock in the first quarter and went back to the locker room with athletic trainers before the Seahawks' second series started. After a slow start, Lock and Seattle made just enough plays to pull off a dramatic 13-10 win .

Darnold was not at the stadium for the rest of the game. He went to nearby Harborview Medical Center for a CT scan on his hip, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter . That test came back inconclusive, and underwent an MRI on Thursday. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said after the game he believed a fracture was ruled out , per ESPN.

The Seahawks believed they avoided a worst-case scenario while they wait on a more definitive timeline.

"At this point, we are able to rule out a fracture," Macdonald said. "So there's some more tests to be done. ... We're still working through all that, but right now I think fracture is out, which is great news."

Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards passing and a 45-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

On the play he was hurt, Darnold was sacked by Patriots end Dre'Mont Jones on a third down on the Seahawks' first drive. As the punt team came on, Darnold was trotting off with a noticeable limp. NBC said on the broadcast that no medical personnel was around Darnold as he came to the sideline, but shortly after he went to the blue medical tent.

After the Patriots punted, NBC showed Darnold limping badly on the sideline as Lock had his helmet on, ready to go in.

Darnold didn't miss a game last season and threw for 4,000 yards in the regular season, then played steady, solid football throughout the Seahawks' Super Bowl championship push. He became a great story of a highly drafted quarterback who was given up on by multiple teams.

As a new season started, another story was unfolding and it wasn't a positive one for the Seahawks or Darnold.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Rams and 49ers go all the way to Australia for opener
articles.summary: The Rams have been the talk of the NFL after a splashy offseason.
articles.body:
The NFL's desire to expand internationally reaches its most aggressive point on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers are traveling a little less than 8,000 miles to play in Melbourne, Australia. It's the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia and one of the biggest challenges teams have faced for international travel. They approached it differently as well.

The 49ers flew to Australia more than a week before the game, while the Rams set a plan to fly in the day before the game . The teams' contrasting travel plans will be a big discussion point after the game, no matter how it turns out.

The NFL didn't send two random teams to Australia, either. The league set up an exciting divisional matchup between the Rams, the clear Super Bowl favorite heading into the season, and their NFC West rival 49ers, coming off a playoff season.

The Rams have been the talk of the offseason. After coming up just short in the NFC championship game, they acquired defensive end and Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett , and cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . Then future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of retirement to join the team, though he won't be playing on Thursday.

Garrett and Matthew Stafford will make history as the first reigning MVP-DPOY combination ever on the same roster. The Rams are loaded and will be fun to watch all season.

Don't rule out the 49ers. San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan has an 11-7 regular-season record against his Rams counterpart Sean McVay, though McVay won the lone playoff matchup. The 49ers have tremendous top-end talent, like quarterback Brock Purdy , running back Christian McCaffrey , offensive tackle Trent Williams , new receiver Mike Evans and tight end George Kittle , who is coming off a torn Achilles.

The Rams will be the headliner in this Week 1 game, as they will be most of the season. The 49ers could help provide a good show in Australia.

Given how much hype the Rams got this offseason, starting 0-1 would lead to a long week of ridicule, and also second-guessing over their travel plan. The Rams will be fine either way, as will the 49ers if they lose, but the talk of the Rams being a runaway favorite will slow down a bit. That might not even be the worst thing, as the Rams probably wouldn't mind a few weeks under the radar even though they'll be in prime time in four of their first five games. But starting the season with a win could set them on a path to a historic season.

Garrett could be the best player, in terms of where he is in his career arc, to be traded through NFL history. He is coming off the single-season sack record and is arguably the best player, regardless of position, in the NFL. The players believe he is indeed No. 1.

The Rams gave up a lot to get Garrett, but it shouldn't take long for everyone to realize what Los Angeles was investing in. Having Garrett playing his first game in prime time, with a rabid NFL fan base excited for the regular season to start, will put an intense focus on his Rams debut. Kyle Shanahan is a smart coach and will have a plan to at least minimize the wreckage Garrett can inflict on San Francisco's offense. But it's a good bet that Garrett makes some impact in his first game with the Rams.

This is a fascinating game from a betting perspective, because how you handicap the differing travel strategies will have a big impact on how you see the game playing out. I asked several oddsmakers both here in the U.S. and in Australia for their thoughts on that topic, and while there was far from a consensus, the general opinion was the Rams' travel itinerary would be better than the 49ers' for both Week 1 and Week 2. The odds have been static for this game — L.A. -3.5 and a total of 48.5 — so it seems like sharp bettors are taking a wait-and-see approach as well. The betting public likes the Rams to cover; I'd side with a few oddsmakers and look to the under.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

There's plenty of fantasy juice in play as the Rams and 49ers get after it in Australia tonight. Here are three things to watch for from a fantasy angle.

1. Can two top offenses buck recent international trends? If you get a little nervous when your fantasy players have an international game, it's justified. Only three of the last 17 games played outside the United States since 2023 have gone over 48 total points.

2. Will the older Niners answer the bell? San Francisco has an intriguing but old offense, with Christian McCaffrey in his age-30 season and Mike Evans and George Kittle negotiating their age-33 laps. All three also have injury concerns to consider; McCaffrey missed time this summer with undisclosed physical issues, Evans dealt with a groin problem, and Kittle is coming back from an Achilles tear in January. With all the age on this depth chart, rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling becomes an intriguing player.

3. How will the Rams handle the backfield? Kyren Williams has been fantasy royalty for three straight seasons, but Blake Corum joined the party down the stretch last year, averaging double-digit carries over the last 11 games. Perhaps both LAR runners can pay off this season, with the Rams a Super Bowl favorite and often headed for positive game scripts (an upgraded defense also helps).
