articles.title: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Pleads No Contest to Misdemeanor Battery Charge
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest Thursday to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his girlfriend.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest Thursday to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his girlfriend.

Jacobs will be fined $1,000 for the battery charge. Under an agreement with prosecutors, the court will suspend the proceedings on the criminal damage charge for 12 months, at which time it will be dismissed upon completion of the terms of the agreement, according to his attorneys.

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after Hobart-Lawrence police officers came to his home to investigate a disturbance. Police said Jacobs' girlfriend told them she had a lump on her head as a result of Jacobs' actions.

He was charged in late August and the NFL subsequently placed Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list, which prevents the three-time Pro Bowl running back from playing or practicing but allows him to keep receiving a paycheck.

Upon request and with the club's permission, players on the commissioner's exempt list may be allowed at the facility for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other non-football activities.

Jacobs is coming off a 2025 season in which he rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Will Return from Injury for Chiefs' Week 1 Game vs. Broncos, Wear Knee Brace
articles.summary: After suffering a torn ACL in Week 15 of the 2025 season, Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes has recovered in time to open the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
After suffering a torn ACL in Week 15 of the 2025 season, Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes has recovered in time to open the 2026 campaign.

On Thursday, Mahomes discussed being available for the Chiefs' Week 1 contest against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football .

"This has always been the goal," he said. "Now I get to go out there and play the sport I love."

He also said he would wear a knee brace.

Kansas City had acquired backup quarterback Justin Fields from the New York Jets over the offseason to fill in for Mahomes when needed, but the two-time NFL MVP is coming back with a vengeance.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid announced before training camp that Mahomes was fully cleared to practice, which was an early sign that things were moving in the right direction. Mahomes later said his knee "feels great," but he was held out of all three of the team's preseason games.

Mahomes and the Chiefs are coming off their worst season in quite some time. Kansas City went 6-11 to finish under .500 for the first time since 2012 and miss the playoffs for the first time since 2014.

In 14 starts, Mahomes threw for 3,587 yards, 22 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. He also added career highs of 422 rushing yards and five scores on the ground, but he sustained 34 sacks, and the physical toll was eventually too much to bear.

The 2025 season wasn't great for Fields, either, as he was benched multiple times by the Jets before being placed on injured reserve in December. He had a 2-7 record in nine games as New York's starter, throwing for 1,259 yards, seven touchdowns and an interception while adding 383 rushing yards and four more scores.

The Chiefs signed star running back and Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III, so he should help take pressure off Mahomes and provide more balance on offense.

Mahomes is clearly motivated to lead the Chiefs back to prominence, and his speedy recovery will surely have fans excited for the season opener against the Broncos.

articles.title: Panthers QB Bryce Young comments on contract situation going into Week 1
articles.summary: Panthers QB Bryce Young was asked about his contract situation heading into the 2026 regular season.
articles.body:
The next major decision facing the Carolina Panthers ' front office will be what to do with their starting quarterback Bryce Young .

Going into his fourth season in the NFL, it's not an easy call. Young has shown flashes of elite ability, but he's still producing at a well below-average level too often.

There are three paths ahead for the organization.

If Young makes his big breakthrough this season, they could give him the lucrative long-term extension that would cement him in as their franchise guy. If he bombs, then they could start looking for another starter, beginning with the loaded draft class of 2027. The Panthers could also decide to wait—if Young's performance falls somewhere in the middle, they still have him under contract for another season thanks to his fifth-year option.

As for Young, he continues to say all the right things. When asked about his contract situation going into Week 1, Young replied that it's out of his hands and he's all about football.

"For me, it's just about football—all that stuff happens. It's outside my control.

"All that stuff, other people and upstairs and agents, all that. It's season time. We're going into Week 1; that's all that matters. We have all the inspiration. There's a great challenge ahead of us, and our first opponent, so that's all that I have the capacity to be focused on."

Young deserves credit for his attitude, which has been in the right place at every turn of his pro career thus far.

When he was benched early in 2024, he was mature and supportive of veteran backup Andy Dalton . When he's had big games and moments, Young has deferred and given credit to his teammates. When he's bombed Young has taken responsibility.

Intangibles like that are great and important for a franchise quarterback, but they're not enough to earn a contract that could be worth $50 million a year. Young has to prove that he can deliver strong results on a consistent basis, or he's not going to get that next big deal from the Panthers.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts and Jayden Daniels with questions to answer in NFL opener as Philadelphia Eagles roll out new offense
articles.summary: Watch Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles take on Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders from 9.25pm, live on Sky Sports NFL; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast throughout the season as Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold discuss the biggest storylines
articles.body:
The Eagles leaned heavily on Vic Fangio's star-studded defense alongside a sputtering Hurts-led attack on the way to winning the NFC East title last season.

It would culminate in a playoff defeat to the San Francisco 49ers and the firing of offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, while a disgruntled AJ Brown departed in the offseason after an apparent breakdown in his connection with Hurts both on and off the field.

"Only Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have accounted for more offensive touchdowns than Jalen Hurts in the last five years," said Reynolds on Inside the Huddle .

"He's a Super Bowl MVP, but those whispers about how he can impact the offense, how he gets along with his team-mates, all of that's grown about as loud as it's ever been during this offseason, about how he can run an offense, what he can do, what his limitations are."

Hurts was named Super Bowl MVP after a commanding performance to lead the Eagles to victory over the Kansas City Chiefs two years ago, denying Andy Reid's side a historic three-peat.

Still, doubts of his talents would follow amid a laboured 2025 campaign.

"It's hard, I think he can be a polarizing character at times because he's actually just so stoic throughout or almost maintains the same emotions. And people want to see him get happy or mad or anything like that," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter.

"I feel like there's so much of other people applying how they feel he should think or feel. Then you have people looking at his career in terms of criticising the run game, criticising his passing game, criticising who he throws the football to, and Philadelphia is not an easy place to play.

"We know that there's a lot of external pressure from the Eagles fans, whether you're winning or losing, but it feels like a team that has consistently been driven by what the outside noise wants, or maybe the coordinators are allowing that to happen where they think, 'oh, they think we need to pass it to this person, they think we should throw it'.

"It almost just needs all those doors shut, which is probably why Jalen Hurts is very much like that. Even spending time with him this offseason he pretty much is exactly the same. He doesn't really get too excited.

"It will be fascinating now, is it that addition by subtraction when it comes to AJ Brown, what does the offense look like?"

Hurts and the Eagles begin their season against another quarterback facing queries in the light of a disappointing campaign marred by injury.

Jayden Daniels missed 10 games for the Washington Commanders last season, failing to build on his Offensive Rookie of the Year-winning campaign.

"He told me in the summer he was going to learn to live to fight another down," said Reynolds. "I will believe it when I see it, once you get in the heat of the battle.

"There's a lot of questions about Jayden Daniels, because if he's healthy, let's not forget two seasons ago, they were in the NFC championship game against these very Eagles."

Schecter added: "Jayden Daniels is so fascinating because he does have such a slim fit frame and we've seen how that can have a negative impact, but we've also seen how his speed and athleticism has really helped the team at times is evasive moves in the pocket, or even just when he's scrambling or running down field.

"And then you've got on top of it, the amount of off-field work that he does from a preparation perspective. The extra meetings that he's doing in the morning to walk through the play script or the virtual reality that he's watching, not every quarterback does that.

"Its just making sure that his offensive line can protect him long enough against an Eagles defense and especially an Eagles defensive line that are just known for their aggression."
